`CHANGELOG.md`:

```md
# Changelog

All notable changes to Aurix Net. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/);
versions follow SemVer. Nodes of one deployment run the same minor version; the `aurix-net:<tag>`
image, the `sbom` artifact and this file's entry are produced from the tagged commit
([release checklist](docs/release-checklist.md)).

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- Unity gameplay framework (`Aurix.Net.Unity.Framework`, `Runtime/Framework/`): host-authoritative
  netcode in the PurrNet/Mirror/FishNet mould over an Aurix relay room — `NetworkManager`
  (`StartHost`/`StartServer`/`StartClient`, prefab registry, `Spawn`/`Despawn`, ownership, tick),
  `NetworkIdentity` (objectId, owner, isServer/isClient/isOwner/isController, despawn on owner
  leave), `NetworkBehaviour` with `SyncVar<T>`, `SyncList<T>`, `SyncDictionary<K,V>` (server- or
  owner-authoritative, per-module send interval, onChanged events, full state on spawn/late join,
  deltas per tick) and `[ServerRpc]` / `[ObserversRpc]` / `[TargetRpc]` methods (requireOwnership,
  runLocally, bufferLast for late joiners, `RpcInfo` sender), `NetSerializer` for primitives, Unity
  math types, strings, byte[], enums, arrays/lists, `PlayerID`, `NetworkIdentity` references and
  `INetSerializable`. Reflection-bound in this version (no IL weaving); `BuildCheck~/framework-check`
  runs host + two clients through spawn, sync, RPCs, ownership transfer, late join and despawn.
- Framework components: `NetworkTransform` (quantized position/rotation/scale from the controller,
  smallest-three quaternions, tick-stamped interpolation buffer, teleport), `NetworkRigidbody`
  (velocities + extrapolation, kinematic remotes) and `NetworkAnimator` (float/int/bool parameters,
  triggers as RPCs); scene objects bound by `NetworkIdentity.sceneId` instead of instantiated;
  a `Hello`/`Welcome` handshake so a joiner gets the world only once its data path is up.
- IL weaver for the framework (`Editor/CodeGen/RpcWeaver.cs`, Mono.Cecil): `[ServerRpc]` /
  `[ObserversRpc]` / `[TargetRpc]` methods become direct call sites (`CmdHit(10)` routes the call,
  the original body moves to `CmdHit__Impl`; `[TargetRpc]` takes the target `PlayerID` as its first
  parameter). Runs in Unity through an `ILPostProcessor` (`Aurix.Net.CodeGen`, editor-only, same
  layout as Netcode for GameObjects — not yet exercised in an editor) and on plain .NET through
  `sdk/unity/Weaver/Aurix.Net.Weaver.Cli` (`aurix-weave <assembly.dll>`), which `framework-check`
  applies to its own test assembly before running the live scenario.
- Interest management: per-object observer sets on the server, `INetworkVisibilityRule`
  (`DistanceRule`, `OwnerOnlyRule`, `AlwaysVisibleRule`, `NoVisibilityRule`, or a per-object rule),
  re-evaluated every `visibilityIntervalTicks`; spawn/despawn, deltas, ObserversRpc and TargetRpc
  follow visibility; owners and the host's player always see their objects.
- `PlayerSpawner` (one owned player object per joiner, round-robin spawn points) and
  `NetworkManager.autoStart` (Host / Server / Client / headless-server-else-client).
- Client-side prediction (`Runtime/Framework/Prediction/PredictedBehaviour<INPUT, STATE>`,
  PurrDiction-style API): the owner samples input per tick, simulates at once, keeps a history and
  sends inputs redundantly; the server simulates the owner's inputs (repeating late ones), applies
  `ServerModifyState` hooks and sends verified states; the owner reconciles on mismatch (rewind +
  replay), observers interpolate (`Interpolate`/`UpdateView`). `serverOnly` modules (inputs) are
  consumed by the server and not relayed.
- Host migration in the framework (`NetworkManager.allowHostMigration`, on by default): when the
  host leaves, the room's new master is promoted to server with the objects it holds (same ids,
  live state), other clients re-attach to it (`RelayBridge.OnPromoted` / `OnHostChanged`).
  Transport adapters keep the old behaviour (disconnect) unless `AllowHostMigration` is set.
- Editor: `NetworkManager` inspector (role, players, tick, objects with owner/observers, Start/Stop
  buttons in play mode), `NetworkIdentity` inspector (stable `sceneId` auto-assigned for scene
  objects from scene + hierarchy path, runtime owner/observers), menu "Aurix Net/Assign scene ids".
  Written against the public UnityEditor API but not yet run in an editor.
- `NetworkTransform.adaptiveSync` (Conservative/Balanced/Aggressive) with pluggable `TransformSyncStrategy` /
  `CompositeTransformSyncStrategy` (`SetSyncStrategy`): the controller skips sends while receivers can reconstruct
  the motion within tolerance (bounded by `maxSendInterval`), receivers extrapolate with the same model.
- `SyncInput<T>` (owner → server only input value with `onChanged`), `SyncTexture` (PNG over `SyncBigData`) and
  `SyncFile` (name + bytes over `SyncBigData`).
- Addressables: `AddressablesPrefabFactory` (compiled when `com.unity.addressables` is present) and the general
  `IAsyncNetworkObjectFactory`: a spawn whose prefab is still loading stays pending on the client together with
  every later message for that object (sync, ownership, RPCs, despawn), then applies in order once loaded.
- Editor: Window ▸ Aurix Net ▸ Network Statistics shows live ping/jitter/throughput/per-player pings
  (written against the public UnityEditor API, not yet run in an Editor).
- Generic RPCs: `[ObserversRpc] void Show<T>(T v)` and friends work; the weaver inserts a prologue that sends the
  call with its type arguments, the receiver closes the method (`MakeGenericMethod`) and deserialises with the
  closed parameter types. Needs the woven assembly (type arguments come from the prologue).
- RPC packing: `compression: RpcCompression.Fast|Balanced|Best` deflates argument payloads when it pays off,
  `deltaPack: true` sends only the XOR/RLE difference from the previous call of the same RPC to the same peer
  (first call to a peer always whole). Available on ServerRpc/ObserversRpc/TargetRpc. Strings up to 64 KB.
- `NetworkManager.statistics` (`NetworkStatistics`): client ping/jitter from periodic pings, per-player ping on the
  server, upload/download bytes and messages per second, high-ping/jitter and stalled-connection events.
- `ValidatedSyncVar<T>`: owner-authoritative value the server checks with `validate(current, proposed)`;
  rejected writes are reverted on the owner (`onRejected`) and never reach observers. Any module can now
  veto owner deltas via `NetworkModule.ReadDeltaFromOwner`.
- `SyncBigData`: chunked replication of large byte payloads (progress + completion events, whole payload to
  late joiners).
- `NetworkBones`: replicates local pose of SkinnedMeshRenderer bones + extra bones (per-bone change mask,
  quantised, smoothed on remotes) for ragdolls/procedural animation.
- `NetworkAudioSource`: volume/pitch/loop/mute/spatial settings as sync vars, Play/Stop/Pause/UnPause/PlayOneShot
  as RPCs, clips by index into a shared list.
- `NetworkReflection`: replicate listed fields/properties of any component or plain object by name (change-mask
  deltas, full state to late joiners) and call its methods over the network via `Invoke(name, args)` with a
  Server/Observers/Target type per method.
- `StateMachine` + `StateNode`/`StateNode<T>`: replicated state machine (server- or owner-authoritative);
  `SetState`, `SetState(node, data)`, `Next`, `Stop`; Enter/Exit/StateUpdate on every peer with the same
  payload, late joiners enter the current state.
- `NetworkLOD`: per-player send-rate tiers by distance (interval per tier, hysteresis, cull beyond the last
  tier); gates module deltas only, visibility/RPCs untouched; `onTierChanged`.
- `StateMachine` + `StateNode`/`StateNode<T>`: replicated state machine (server- or owner-authoritative);
  `SetState`, `SetState(node, data)`, `Next`, `Stop`; Enter/Exit/StateUpdate on every peer with the same
  payload, late joiners enter the current state.
- `NetworkLOD`: per-player send-rate tiers by distance (interval per tier, hysteresis, cull beyond the last
  tier); gates module deltas only, visibility/RPCs untouched; `onTierChanged`.
- `NetworkTransform.syncParent` + `SetParent(NetworkIdentity)`: the parent object id travels with the
  pose, remotes re-parent and apply the pose in the parent's local space while attached.
- Static RPCs: `[ServerRpc]`/`[ObserversRpc]`/`[TargetRpc]` on static methods of any class, routed via
  `NetworkManager.main` (the active manager; `SetMain` to pick one); identified on the wire by an FNV-1a
  hash of type/method/arg-count so the weaver and runtime agree across assemblies; `bufferLast` replays
  to late joiners. Weaver handles them (`__StaticRpcSend`, `__StaticLocalInfo`).
- Lag compensation: `ColliderRollback` keeps a per-tick pose history on the server; clients report
  their view tick (`viewDelayTicks` behind the newest server tick, `Msg.ViewTick`) and the server
  broadcasts its clock every tick; `NetworkManager.Rollback(shooter, body)` rewinds all rollback
  components to the shooter's view tick around `body` and restores them.
- Sync modules: `SyncHashSet<T>`, `SyncQueue<T>`, `SyncArray<T>` (changed slots only), `SyncEvent<T>`
  (fire-and-forget payload, not replayed to late joiners) and `SyncTimer` (server-tick countdown,
  `remaining`/`finished`/`Poll()`), same authority/full/delta rules as `SyncList`.
- Quick match: `NetworkManager.StartAuto()` joins a random open room matching `matchFilterJson` /
  `matchExpr` as a client, or hosts a fresh room with `roomPropsJson` when none exists
  (`RelayBridge.StartAuto()`; the same settings are available to the transport adapters).
- Unity: transports for third-party netcode over an Aurix relay room — `AurixNetTransport`
  (PurrNet `GenericTransport`/`ITransport`), `AurixNetMirrorTransport` (Mirror `Transport`) and
  `AurixNetFishNetTransport` (FishNet `Transport`) on a shared `RelayBridge`: the host is the room
  master, host→client frames are targeted events, client→host frames go to the master, connection
  ids are actor ids, reliable channels ride the reliable relay channel (fragmented above the
  datagram size), kicks map to the framework's disconnect. Compiled only when the framework is
  present (`AURIX_PURRNET` version define for `dev.purrnet.purrnet`, Mirror's `MIRROR`, FishNet's
  `FISHNET`). No host migration yet. `BuildCheck~/transports-check` runs host + two clients through
  each adapter against a local node.
- `get_rooms{expr?, limit?}`: one-shot filtered room list on the control channel (SQL-lobby
  style filter); Web `client.rooms()`, C# `RoomsAsync`.
- WebRPC: `rpc{id, name, body}` on the control channel calls the project's webhook subscribed to
  `rpc` (signed POST, 5 s, ≤ 16 KiB answer) and returns `rpc_result`; Web `client.rpc()`, C#
  `RpcAsync`, Rust `Client::rpc`. 5 calls/s per session, body ≤ 8 KiB.
- Sync (owner-authoritative rooms): clients can `spawn`/`write`/`despawn`/`transfer` entities they
  own (op list input, ≤ 32 spawned per actor); a leaving actor's entities are despawned. Web
  `SyncClient.spawn/despawn/transfer/writeEntity`, C# `SyncWorld.EncodeOps`/`SyncOp`, C ABI
  `aurix_net_sync_send_op` (C++ `Sync::spawn/despawn/transfer/writeEntity`).

### Fixed
- Re-hosting: two players rejoining the same orphaned room through one node at the same time could
  end up in two rooms of the same name (the row was mistaken for a crash leftover while the
  adoption was still in flight). The node now tracks in-flight adoptions, concurrent joins get
  `room_pending` and retry for up to 2 s; `join` retries too. Found on a two-host run
  ([docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md), Multi-host).

### CI
- `release.yml`: tag-driven release (version/CHANGELOG check, server bundles for linux
  x86_64/aarch64, SDK archives, SBOM, multi-arch GHCR images, GitHub Release with checksums).
  `soak.yml`: nightly 10-minute two-node soak with RSS/overrun verdict and the CSV attached.
- Docker job loads the built images into the daemon before the Trivy scan; the Godot
  GDExtension step builds `libaurix_net` first.

## [0.1.0] — first release candidate

One game-agnostic networking service — relay, sync and lockstep rooms in the same node — plus a
deterministic simulation toolkit, SDKs for Web/Unity/C++/Godot, an operator console and a
self-host deployment. Everything below is verified locally (see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)).

### Node (`aurix-net-server`)
- Transport: QUIC datagrams natively, WebTransport (HTTP/3) with a WebSocket binary fallback in
  browsers; reliable/unreliable/reliable-unordered channels, fragmentation (64 KiB), coalescing,
  per-datagram batching; control plane over WebSocket JSON and REST (Axum).
- Relay rooms: events with target groups, interest groups, event cache (room/slot/slices),
  room and player props with TTL, master client, slot takeover, spectators, kick, lobby
  statistics (`stats`), friend presence (`find_friends`), webhooks with HMAC + SSRF guards.
- Sync rooms: server-authoritative `Frame` (entities, schema components, bit codec, deltas,
  acks, lag-compensation history), owner-authoritative writes, AOI grid with priority budgets and
  `set_view` viewpoints/interest, simulation events, optional server-side WASM room logic.
- Lockstep rooms: server clock, redundant input bundles, canonical journal (Redis), late join
  with checkpoints, desync detection with reference dumps, predict/rollback runner, and a
  **referee**: the node runs the room's WASM simulation itself (Wasmtime, fuel/memory/log budgets)
  and its state is the truth (`referee: true`, actor `0` dump).
- Matchmaking: Redis-backed tickets shared across nodes, leader-locked cycle, attrs + SQL-like
  filters, bot backfill, `fill_existing`.
- Multi-node: Postgres + Redis, per-node heartbeat liveness, drain/handoff on `SIGTERM`,
  rolling upgrades, rehost/rejoin, regions as a first-class field, cross-node operator calls.
- Security: API keys (SHA-256, scopes, expiry, CIDR allow-lists), short-lived player grants with
  secret rotation (`grant_secret_previous`), named operator tokens, audit log of every mutation,
  quotas and monthly caps per project, bounded decoders fuzz-tested (`tests/garbage.rs`), JSON
  depth/size limits, `/metrics` behind a token.
- Operations: `--migrate-only`, `--healthcheck`, Prometheus alert rules, backup script
  (pg_dump + Redis RDB + SHA-256 manifest), distroless non-root image (62.6 MB), hardened compose
  (read-only rootfs, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `no-new-privileges`), Caddy TLS example, SBOM + Trivy +
  `cargo deny` in CI, mimalloc allocator.

### aurix-sim (deterministic, Q32.32 fixed point, native == wasm32)
- `net-fpmath` (vec2/vec3/quat/mat3/RNG), `net-sim` (ECS frame, snapshot/restore/hash).
- `net-sim-physics` 2D: circles/boxes/polygons/capsules, joints (distance/revolute/weld),
  character controller, ray/circle casts, contact events.
- `net-sim-physics3d`: spheres/capsules/boxes/convex hulls (SAT + face clipping), ball/hinge/
  distance joints, kinematic capsule character controller, ray/sphere/capsule/box sweeps.
- `net-sim-nav`: navmesh import, A* + funnel, raycast on mesh, flow fields, crowd steering.
- `net-sim-bots`: behavior trees + HFSM + blackboard (Rust, with TS and C# ports sharing JSON vectors).
- One flat ABI (`net-sim-wasm`, 98 functions) for Web/Unity (wasm/native) and C/C++/Godot
  (`aurix_sim.h`); six golden hashes checked native == wasm32 in CI.

### SDKs
- Web (`@aurix/net`): relay/sync/lockstep clients, rollback runner, matchmaking, presence,
  Sim wrappers; 28 tests incl. live ones.
- Unity (UPM): P/Invoke client, `NetRunner`/`NetView`/`SyncBehaviour`, `NetTransform`,
  `NetRigidbody`, `NetAnimator`, `TickTimer`, spawn hooks, lockstep client + rollback, Sim wrappers;
  managed tests under dotnet (editor run pending a licence).
- Rust (`net-client`), CLI (`aurix-net`), C ABI (`libaurix_net` + `aurix_net.h`/`aurix_sim.h`),
  C++ header-only wrapper, Godot 4 GDExtension (relay + sync, verified headless).
- Operator console (React/Vite SPA behind Caddy): projects, keys, quotas, rooms, nodes, desync
  dumps, matchmaking queue, usage CSV, attention panel; Playwright suite against a live node.

### Not in scope
- Unreal SDK (the engine ships its own netcode), client-hosted P2P topologies, coupling with
  Aurix Voice (a separate service a game uses independently).

`Dockerfile`:

```
# Production image for the Aurix Net node: static-ish release build, non-root, SIGTERM drains
# (rooms are checkpointed and handed to another node), /healthz drives the container healthcheck.
FROM rust:1-bookworm AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY . .
RUN cargo build --release -p net-server --locked

# Distroless runtime: glibc + CA roots only, no shell, no package manager (bookworm-slim carried
# ~46 unfixed HIGH CVEs in util-linux/curl that the node never uses). Runs as uid 65532 (nonroot).
FROM gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12:nonroot
COPY --from=build /src/target/release/aurix-net-server /usr/local/bin/aurix-net-server
WORKDIR /
# HTTP/WS control plane, QUIC and WebTransport datagrams.
EXPOSE 8090/tcp 7000/udp 7443/udp
# Containers are reached through published ports, so the control plane must bind all interfaces
# (the binary defaults to 127.0.0.1:8090 for bare-metal dev runs).
ENV NET__SERVER__HTTP_ADDR=0.0.0.0:8090
# Configuration: built-in defaults, optionally `--config /etc/aurix-net/net.toml` (mount it),
# and NET__SECTION__KEY environment overrides (e.g. NET__AUTH__GRANT_SECRET).
STOPSIGNAL SIGTERM
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
    CMD ["/usr/local/bin/aurix-net-server", "--healthcheck"]
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/aurix-net-server"]

```

`README.md`:

```md
<p align="center"><img src="assets/logo.svg" width="72" height="72" alt="Aurix Net"></p>
<h1 align="center">Aurix Net</h1>
<p align="center">
  <a href="https://github.com/aurix-voice/aurix-net/actions/workflows/ci.yml"><img alt="CI" src="https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/aurix-voice/aurix-net/ci.yml?branch=main&label=ci"></a>
  <a href="https://github.com/aurix-voice/aurix-net/releases"><img alt="Release" src="https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/aurix-voice/aurix-net?label=release&color=0a0a0a"></a>
  <a href="LICENSE"><img alt="License" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0%20%2B%20Apache--2.0%20SDKs-0a0a0a"></a>
</p>

Open-source, self-hosted game networking — relay rooms, server-authoritative state sync and
deterministic lockstep in one node, with matchmaking, replays and a server-side referee. One
server, one client library, three room modes; you pick per room.

Don't want to run it yourself? **[Aurix Cloud](https://aurix.run/net/)** hosts the same node: a
free tier with no card, [docs](https://aurix.run/docs/net/), tiers priced per project and never per
player. Your servers, our control plane — also possible. Aurix Net is the companion of
[Aurix Voice](https://github.com/aurix-voice/aurix); the two are separate services a game uses
independently.

* **Three room modes in one node** — `relay` (events, targets, interest groups, event cache,
  room/player props with TTL, master client, slot takeover, spectators), `sync` (server-owned
  `Frame` of entities and schema components, bit codec with deltas, owner-authoritative writes,
  area-of-interest with priority budgets, lag compensation) and `lockstep` (server clock,
  redundant input bundles, canonical journal, late join from checkpoints, desync detection with
  reference dumps, predict/rollback). Rooms move to another node when one dies; they do not die.
* **Referee** — a room's WASM simulation runs on the node itself (Wasmtime, fuel/memory/log
  budgets) and its state is the truth; the same module runs in every client.
* **Transport** — QUIC datagrams natively, WebTransport (HTTP/3) with a binary WebSocket
  fallback in browsers; reliable / unreliable / reliable-unordered channels, fragmentation,
  coalescing, per-datagram batching; JSON control channel over WebSocket and a REST API.
* **Matchmaking, lobbies, presence** — Redis-backed tickets shared across nodes, attribute and
  SQL-like filters, bot backfill, `fill_existing`; lobby statistics, friend presence, one-shot
  filtered room lists; webhooks with HMAC signatures and WebRPC calls into your backend.
* **Replays** — journals of lockstep rooms, instant-replay windows from live rooms (kill cam),
  stored replays with retention per project.
* **aurix-sim** — deterministic simulation kit in Q32.32 fixed point, identical on native and
  wasm32: 2D and 3D rigid-body physics with joints and character controllers, ray/shape casts,
  navmesh (A* + funnel, flow fields, crowd steering) and bots (behaviour trees, HFSM,
  blackboard), one flat ABI for every SDK.
* **Multi-tenant and multi-node** — projects, API keys (hashed, scoped, expiring, CIDR-bound),
  short-lived player grants with secret rotation, named operator tokens, quotas and monthly caps,
  audit log of every mutation; PostgreSQL + Redis control plane, heartbeat liveness, drain and
  handoff on `SIGTERM`, rolling upgrades, regions as a first-class field.
* **Ops** — operator console (projects, keys, quotas, rooms, nodes, desync dumps, matchmaking
  queue, usage CSV), Prometheus metrics and alert rules, backup script, distroless non-root
  image, hardened Compose, Caddy TLS example, SBOM + Trivy + `cargo deny` in CI.

> **Status: 0.1.0** — relay, sync and lockstep rooms, the referee, matchmaking, aurix-sim and the
> SDKs for Web, Unity, Rust, C/C++ and Godot; every piece is exercised by CI against a live node
> ([docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)). Not in scope: an Unreal SDK (the engine ships its own
> netcode) and client-hosted P2P topologies.

**Documentation**: [room modes](docs/modes.md) · [API: keys, grants, REST, control channel, data
path, webhooks, matchmaking, modules](docs/api.md) · [SDK guide](docs/sdk.md) ·
[webhooks](docs/webhooks.md) · [deployment](docs/deployment.md) · [testing](docs/testing.md) ·
[aurix-sim design](docs/sim/design.md) · [release checklist](docs/release-checklist.md).

---

## Quick start

```bash
docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.dev.yml up -d        # PostgreSQL + Redis
cargo build --release
NET__AUTH__ADMIN_TOKEN=change-me ./target/release/aurix-net-server

# create a project (the response carries its first API key)
curl -s -X POST localhost:8090/v1/operator/projects -H 'Authorization: Bearer change-me' \
     -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"demo"}'

# load test: 100 rooms x 10 players, 20 events/s each, over QUIC
./target/release/aurix-net-loadtest --api-key an_... --rooms 100 --players 10 --rate 20
```

Config is a TOML file (`--config`); every key can be overridden as `NET__SECTION__KEY`
([config.rs](crates/net-common/src/config.rs)). Two roles run a deployment: the **operator**
(whoever hosts the nodes — quotas, drain, suspend, usage) and **projects** (API keys scoped to one
game). Self-hosting means you are both — [who does what](docs/api.md#who-does-what-operator-vs-project).

**How a client gets in**: it opens the WebSocket control channel (`/ws`), authenticates with a
grant your backend issued (`POST /v1/grants` with the project's API key) and joins a room. The node
answers with a data endpoint (host, QUIC port, certificate fingerprint, 30-second ticket); the
client connects over QUIC, sends the ticket as its first datagram, and game events travel as
datagrams from then on. Where UDP is blocked the same datagrams ride as binary WebSocket frames.

## Client SDKs

| SDK | Path | What |
|---|---|---|
| Web (TypeScript) | [`sdk/web`](sdk/web) | `@aurix/net`: relay / sync / lockstep clients, rollback runner, matchmaking, presence, instant replay, aurix-sim (wasm) |
| Unity (UPM, pure C#) | [`sdk/unity`](sdk/unity) | every platform incl. WebGL: `NetRunner` / `NetView` / `SyncBehaviour`, `NetTransform`, `NetRigidbody`, `NetAnimator`, lockstep + rollback, a host-authoritative gameplay framework (`NetworkManager`, `NetworkBehaviour`, RPCs, SyncVars, LOD, spawning) and transports for PurrNet, Mirror and FishNet over relay rooms |
| Rust | [`crates/net-client`](crates/net-client) | control + data path, rollback, replays; the reference client |
| C / C++ | [`crates/net-ffi`](crates/net-ffi), [`sdk/cpp`](sdk/cpp) | `libaurix_net` C ABI (`aurix_net.h`, `aurix_sim.h`) and a header-only C++ wrapper |
| Godot 4 (GDExtension) | [`sdk/godot`](sdk/godot) | `AurixNetClient` node over the C ABI: relay, sync and lockstep rooms, aurix-sim |

All SDKs authenticate with a short-lived grant from `POST /v1/grants`; API keys stay on your backend.
The `aurix-net` CLI ([`crates/net-cli`](crates/net-cli)) covers projects, keys, rooms, modules and
usage from a terminal; [`crates/net-loadtest`](crates/net-loadtest) drives relay / sync / lockstep bots
with loss, latency and tick reports.

## Layout

| Crate | Role |
|---|---|
| `net-common` | ids, errors, config, protocol limits |
| `net-transport` | 12-byte datagram header, channels (unreliable-sequenced, reliable-ordered, reliable-unordered) with own acks/retransmits, fragmentation, batching, QUIC endpoints (pinned certs), data tickets |
| `net-auth` | API keys (SHA-256 at rest), join grants (JWT HS256), operator token |
| `net-db` | PostgreSQL (sqlx), migrations in `migrations/` |
| `net-control` | node registry/placement, project quotas, Redis live room directory + lobby pub/sub |
| `net-rooms` | relay room logic: membership, props with CAS, events/targets/groups/cache, master, kick, offline slots |
| `net-api` | WebSocket control channel, QUIC data plane, REST + operator API, webhooks, matchmaking, metrics |
| `net-game` | server-side WASM room logic and the lockstep referee |
| `net-server` | the node binary `aurix-net-server` |
| `net-wire` | schema IDL, bit codec, quantization, deltas |
| `net-sim`, `net-sim-physics`, `net-sim-physics3d`, `net-sim-nav`, `net-sim-bots`, `net-sim-wasm` | aurix-sim: ECS frame, 2D/3D physics, navmesh, bots, the flat ABI |
| `net-replication` | per-client baselines, AOI, priority, delta build/apply |
| `net-lagcomp` | hitbox history, rewind raycasts |
| `net-fpmath` | Q32.32 fixed point, deterministic trig and RNG |
| `net-rollback` | prediction, rollback, hashes, replays |
| `net-client`, `net-ffi`, `net-cli`, `net-loadtest` | Rust client, C ABI, command line, bots |
| `dashboard/` | operator console (Vite + React), shipped as its own image |

`SECURITY.md`:

```md
# Security

## Reporting

Email security@aurix.dev (PGP key on the website). We acknowledge within 2 business days and
aim to ship fixes for confirmed issues within 14 days. Please do not open public issues for
vulnerabilities.

## Threat model

Aurix Net nodes are reachable from the public internet on three ports (HTTP control plane,
QUIC data, WebTransport data). We assume:

- **Game clients are hostile.** Anything a client can send is validated for size, rate and
  semantics; a client can only act as the player its grant names, inside the room it joined.
- **Tenants (projects) are mutually untrusted.** Projects are isolated by API key / grant; a
  project's WASM logic runs in a sandbox with fuel, memory and module-size caps and cannot
  reach the host, other rooms or the network.
- **The node's own infrastructure (Postgres, Redis, other nodes) is trusted** and must live on
  a private network (see `docs/deployment.md`).

## Controls

| Area | Control |
|---|---|
| API keys | stored as SHA-256 hashes; `an_<prefix>_<secret>` format; scopes (`rooms`, `read`, `admin`); per-key write budget (`limits.writes_per_sec_per_key`) |
| Operator token | constant-time comparison; empty token disables operator endpoints |
| Grants | HS256 JWT signed with `auth.grant_secret` (≥ 32 random bytes enforced outside development); `exp` checked with 5 s leeway; scopes limited to `join/create/master/spectate`; `room` binding; `meta` ≤ 1 KiB; control characters stripped |
| Data tickets | HMAC-SHA256 over session/room/actor, 30 s TTL; constant-time check; a stale data session cannot act on a slot a newer one owns |
| Transport | QUIC/WebTransport over TLS 1.3 with certificate pinning (`cert_sha256`) for self-signed deployments; QUIC Retry (address validation) before any handshake work; per-IP connection cap |
| Control plane | per-IP HTTP budget, per-IP WebSocket connect budget, auth-failure budget per IP (shared by WebSocket grant failures and REST 401s on API keys / operator tokens; spent budget turns 401 into 429, valid callers unaffected), 10 s pre-auth timeout, 8 KiB pre-auth message cap, 90 s idle timeout, 64 KiB body cap (8 MiB for module upload) |
| Rooms | room/player props size caps, per-room and per-player event budgets, input-rate and look-ahead caps, max players per room/node, project quotas |
| Webhooks | https only outside development, no credentials in URL, no redirects, private/loopback/link-local/metadata hosts refused both at registration and at delivery (DNS rebinding) |
| WASM | wasmtime with fuel (50 M per call), 64 MiB memory, 8 MiB module; a trapping module is disabled, the node is unaffected |
| Shutdown | SIGTERM/Ctrl-C drains: fresh checkpoints to Redis, rooms become `orphaned` for another node to adopt, `/healthz` answers 503 |
| Dependencies | `cargo audit` / `cargo deny` clean (see `deny.toml`) |

## Not covered (by design)

- Cheating inside the rules of a game: that is the job of server-authoritative logic (sync
  mode, WASM) or deterministic verification (lockstep with a server-stepped module).
- DDoS at volumetric scale: put nodes behind your provider's L3/L4 protection; the node
  limits above handle application-level floods.
- Grants are bearer tokens: anyone holding a grant is that player until it expires. Issue
  them with short TTLs from your backend only.

### Per-IP limits and shared addresses

Per-IP budgets are DoS backstops, not fairness controls: whole campuses, mobile carriers (CGNAT) and
LAN parties sit behind one address, so the defaults are deliberately loose (512 sessions, 200 HTTP
requests/s, 600 WebSocket connects/min, 20 failed auths/min per IP) and verified with a 128-player
join burst from a single host. Project quotas (`max_rooms`, `max_players_per_room`, per-room/per-player event rates, event bytes)
and per-player input budgets carry the per-tenant fairness; grant minting has its own per-key budget
(`grants_per_sec_per_key`, 500/s) because it is every player login of the tenant's backend; tune `[limits]` down only behind a proxy that passes
`X-Forwarded-For` from `server.trusted_proxies`.

`crates/net-api/src/alerts.rs`:

```rs
//! Fleet alerts: one node (Redis leader lock) re-evaluates the operator attention list every
//! minute and emits each item to the operator webhooks at most once per hour per subject.

use crate::state::Shared;
use std::time::Duration;

const LEADER_KEY: &str = "aurix:alerts:leader";
const LEADER_TTL_MS: u64 = 90_000;
const REPEAT_SECS: u64 = 3600;

pub async fn run(st: Shared) {
    let mut iv = tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(60));
    loop {
        iv.tick().await;
        if let Err(e) = cycle(&st).await {
            tracing::warn!(error = %e, "alert cycle failed");
        }
    }
}

async fn is_leader(st: &Shared) -> anyhow::Result<bool> {
    let mut c = st.redis.raw();
    let node = st.node_id.to_string();
    let got: Option<String> = redis::cmd("SET")
        .arg(LEADER_KEY)
        .arg(&node)
        .arg("NX")
        .arg("PX")
        .arg(LEADER_TTL_MS)
        .query_async(&mut c)
        .await?;
    if got.is_some() {
        return Ok(true);
    }
    let leader: Option<String> = redis::cmd("GET")
        .arg(LEADER_KEY)
        .query_async(&mut c)
        .await?;
    if leader.as_deref() == Some(node.as_str()) {
        let _: () = redis::cmd("PEXPIRE")
            .arg(LEADER_KEY)
            .arg(LEADER_TTL_MS)
            .query_async(&mut c)
            .await?;
        return Ok(true);
    }
    Ok(false)
}

/// True the first time a subject is seen within `REPEAT_SECS`.
async fn first_time(st: &Shared, key: &str) -> anyhow::Result<bool> {
    let mut c = st.redis.raw();
    let got: Option<String> = redis::cmd("SET")
        .arg(format!("aurix:alert:{key}"))
        .arg("1")
        .arg("NX")
        .arg("EX")
        .arg(REPEAT_SECS)
        .query_async(&mut c)
        .await?;
    Ok(got.is_some())
}

async fn cycle(st: &Shared) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    if !is_leader(st).await? {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let att = crate::rest::attention_value(st)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e.to_string()))?;
    let mut items: Vec<(&'static str, String, serde_json::Value)> = Vec::new();
    let arr = |k: &str| att[k].as_array().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    for n in arr("stale_nodes") {
        items.push(("node.stale", n["id"].to_string(), n));
    }
    for n in arr("draining_nodes") {
        items.push(("node.draining", n["id"].to_string(), n));
    }
    for p in arr("suspended_projects") {
        items.push(("project.suspended", p["id"].to_string(), p));
    }
    for w in arr("failing_webhooks") {
        items.push(("webhook.failing", w["webhook_id"].to_string(), w));
    }
    for u in arr("usage_caps") {
        let hard = u["used"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0) >= u["cap"].as_f64().unwrap_or(f64::MAX);
        let key = format!(
            "{}:{}:{}",
            u["project_id"],
            u["metric"],
            if hard { "hard" } else { "soft" }
        );
        let mut u = u;
        u["hard"] = serde_json::Value::Bool(hard);
        items.push(("project.usage_cap", key, u));
    }
    for r in arr("rejections") {
        items.push(("project.rejections", r["project_id"].to_string(), r));
    }
    for (event, subject, payload) in items {
        if first_time(st, &format!("{event}:{subject}")).await? {
            st.webhooks.emit_fleet(event, payload);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

`crates/net-api/src/data.rs`:

```rs
//! QUIC data plane: the first datagram of a connection is the data ticket; everything after
//! runs through the session's [`Link`].

use crate::host::{handle_data_frame, DataSession, DataSink};
use crate::state::Shared;
use crate::ws::{attach_data, spawn_ticker};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

pub async fn run_quic(st: Shared, endpoint: quinn::Endpoint) {
    while let Some(incoming) = endpoint.accept().await {
        // Address validation before any handshake work: no amplification from spoofed sources.
        if !incoming.remote_address_validated() {
            let _ = incoming.retry();
            continue;
        }
        let ip = incoming.remote_address().ip();
        if !st.guards.acquire_session(ip) {
            st.metrics.errors.with_label_values(&["rate_limited"]).inc();
            incoming.refuse();
            continue;
        }
        let st = st.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            if let Err(e) = handle(st.clone(), incoming).await {
                tracing::debug!(error = %e, "quic connection ended");
            }
            st.guards.release_session(ip);
        });
    }
}

async fn handle(st: Shared, incoming: quinn::Incoming) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let conn = incoming.await?;
    let first = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), conn.read_datagram()).await??;
    let Some(t) = st.tickets.verify(&first) else {
        conn.close(1u32.into(), b"bad ticket");
        anyhow::bail!("bad ticket");
    };
    let Some(h) = st.host.get(t.room) else {
        conn.close(2u32.into(), b"no room");
        anyhow::bail!("no such room");
    };
    {
        let g = h.lock();
        if !g.sessions.contains_key(&t.actor) {
            drop(g);
            conn.close(3u32.into(), b"not joined");
            anyhow::bail!("actor not joined");
        }
    }
    let ds = DataSession::new(DataSink::Quic(conn.clone()), st.metrics.clone());
    let ds = attach_data(&h, t.actor, ds);
    spawn_ticker(&st, ds.clone());
    loop {
        let d = match conn.read_datagram().await {
            Ok(d) => d,
            Err(_) => break,
        };
        for m in ds.receive(d) {
            if m.payload.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let mut g = h.lock();
            // A newer connection (reconnect or another session of the player) owns the slot.
            if !g
                .sessions
                .get(&t.actor)
                .and_then(|a| a.data.as_ref())
                .is_some_and(|d| Arc::ptr_eq(d, &ds))
            {
                return Ok(());
            }
            if let Err(e) = handle_data_frame(&mut g, t.actor, m.channel, m.payload, &st.metrics) {
                st.metrics.errors.with_label_values(&[e.code()]).inc();
            }
        }
    }
    // Detach only if we are still the active data session.
    let mut g = h.lock();
    if let Some(a) = g.sessions.get_mut(&t.actor) {
        if a.data.as_ref().is_some_and(|d| Arc::ptr_eq(d, &ds)) {
            a.data = None;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// WebTransport data plane: identical protocol to [`run_quic`] (ticket first, then datagrams
/// through the session's link), reached by browsers via `joined.data.webtransport_url`.
pub async fn run_webtransport(
    st: Shared,
    endpoint: wtransport::Endpoint<wtransport::endpoint::endpoint_side::Server>,
) {
    loop {
        let incoming = endpoint.accept().await;
        let ip = incoming.remote_address().ip();
        if !st.guards.acquire_session(ip) {
            st.metrics.errors.with_label_values(&["rate_limited"]).inc();
            continue;
        }
        let st = st.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            if let Err(e) = handle_wt(st.clone(), incoming).await {
                tracing::debug!(error = %e, "webtransport session ended");
            }
            st.guards.release_session(ip);
        });
    }
}

async fn handle_wt(
    st: Shared,
    incoming: wtransport::endpoint::IncomingSession,
) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let request = incoming.await?;
    let conn = request.accept().await?;
    let first = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), conn.receive_datagram()).await??;
    let Some(t) = st.tickets.verify(&first.payload()) else {
        conn.close(1u32.into(), b"bad ticket");
        anyhow::bail!("bad ticket");
    };
    let Some(h) = st.host.get(t.room) else {
        conn.close(2u32.into(), b"no room");
        anyhow::bail!("no such room");
    };
    if !h.lock().sessions.contains_key(&t.actor) {
        conn.close(3u32.into(), b"not joined");
        anyhow::bail!("actor not joined");
    }
    let ds = DataSession::new(DataSink::WebTransport(conn.clone()), st.metrics.clone());
    let ds = attach_data(&h, t.actor, ds);
    spawn_ticker(&st, ds.clone());
    loop {
        let d = match conn.receive_datagram().await {
            Ok(d) => d.payload(),
            Err(_) => break,
        };
        for m in ds.receive(d) {
            if m.payload.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let mut g = h.lock();
            // A newer connection (reconnect or another session of the player) owns the slot.
            if !g
                .sessions
                .get(&t.actor)
                .and_then(|a| a.data.as_ref())
                .is_some_and(|d| Arc::ptr_eq(d, &ds))
            {
                return Ok(());
            }
            if let Err(e) = handle_data_frame(&mut g, t.actor, m.channel, m.payload, &st.metrics) {
                tracing::debug!(error = %e, "bad data frame (webtransport)");
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

`crates/net-api/src/host.rs`:

```rs
//! Rooms hosted on this node and the sessions attached to them.

use crate::metrics::Metrics;
use bytes::Bytes;
use dashmap::DashMap;
use net_common::{ActorId, Channel, NetError, ProjectId, Result, RoomId};
use net_rooms::protocol::ServerMsg;
use net_rooms::{EventFrame, Outgoing, Room};
use net_transport::Link;
use parking_lot::Mutex;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Instant;
use tokio::sync::mpsc;

/// Where a session's datagrams go.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub enum DataSink {
    Quic(quinn::Connection),
    /// WebTransport session (browsers): HTTP/3 datagrams over QUIC.
    WebTransport(wtransport::Connection),
    /// Binary WebSocket frames (tunnel mode).
    Ws(mpsc::Sender<Bytes>),
}

pub struct DataSession {
    pub link: Mutex<Link>,
    pub sink: DataSink,
    pub metrics: Arc<Metrics>,
    /// Byte counters already billed by the metering task (see `metering.rs`).
    pub metered_in: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64,
    pub metered_out: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64,
}

impl DataSession {
    pub fn new(sink: DataSink, metrics: Arc<Metrics>) -> Arc<Self> {
        Arc::new(Self {
            link: Mutex::new(Link::new(Instant::now())),
            sink,
            metrics,
            metered_in: Default::default(),
            metered_out: Default::default(),
        })
    }

    /// Queues a message and flushes everything the link produced.
    pub fn send(&self, channel: Channel, payload: Bytes) {
        let out: Vec<Bytes> = {
            let mut l = self.link.lock();
            if l.send(channel, payload, Instant::now()).is_err() {
                return;
            }
            // Unreliable messages are coalesced and leave on the next flusher pass.
            if channel == Channel::UnreliableSequenced {
                return;
            }
            std::iter::from_fn(|| l.next_outgoing()).collect()
        };
        self.flush(out);
    }

    pub fn flush(&self, out: Vec<Bytes>) {
        for d in out {
            self.metrics.datagrams_out.inc();
            self.metrics.bytes_out.inc_by(d.len() as u64);
            let ok = match &self.sink {
                DataSink::Quic(c) => match c.send_datagram(d) {
                    Ok(()) => true,
                    Err(quinn::SendDatagramError::TooLarge) => {
                        tracing::warn!(max = ?c.max_datagram_size(), "datagram too large for path");
                        false
                    }
                    Err(_) => false,
                },
                DataSink::WebTransport(c) => c.send_datagram(d).is_ok(),
                DataSink::Ws(tx) => tx.try_send(d).is_ok(),
            };
            if !ok {
                self.metrics
                    .errors
                    .with_label_values(&["datagram_send"])
                    .inc();
            }
        }
    }

    /// Feeds a datagram; returns decoded application messages.
    pub fn receive(&self, d: Bytes) -> Vec<net_transport::Received> {
        self.metrics.datagrams_in.inc();
        self.metrics.bytes_in.inc_by(d.len() as u64);
        let (recv, out) = {
            let mut l = self.link.lock();
            let r = l.receive(d, Instant::now());
            let _ = l.poll(Instant::now());
            (
                r,
                std::iter::from_fn(|| l.next_outgoing()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            )
        };
        self.flush(out);
        recv
    }

    /// Timer-driven retransmits/acks. Returns false when the link is dead.
    pub fn tick(&self) -> bool {
        let (alive, out) = {
            let mut l = self.link.lock();
            let alive = l.poll(Instant::now()).is_ok();
            (
                alive,
                std::iter::from_fn(|| l.next_outgoing()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            )
        };
        self.flush(out);
        alive
    }
}

pub struct Attached {
    pub control: mpsc::Sender<ServerMsg>,
    /// Control session owning this slot; a newer session of the same player replaces it.
    pub session: net_common::SessionId,
    pub data: Option<Arc<DataSession>>,
}

pub struct HostedRoom {
    pub room: Room,
    pub sessions: HashMap<ActorId, Attached>,
    pub project: ProjectId,
    /// Present for rooms in sync mode.
    pub sync: Option<crate::sync::SyncRoom>,
    /// Present for rooms in lockstep mode.
    pub lockstep: Option<crate::lockstep::LockstepRoom>,
}

pub const FLUSH_EVERY: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_millis(2);

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct RoomHost {
    /// Every live data session; the flusher drives retransmits, acks and batches.
    data_sessions: Mutex<Vec<std::sync::Weak<DataSession>>>,
    rooms: DashMap<RoomId, Arc<Mutex<HostedRoom>>>,
    by_name: DashMap<(ProjectId, String), RoomId>,
    /// Lobby subscribers per project on this node.
    lobby: DashMap<ProjectId, Vec<mpsc::Sender<ServerMsg>>>,
    /// Authenticated control sessions per (project, player) — presence for `find_friends`.
    presence: DashMap<(ProjectId, String), u32>,
}

impl RoomHost {
    pub fn register_data(&self, ds: &Arc<DataSession>) {
        self.data_sessions.lock().push(Arc::downgrade(ds));
    }

    /// One pass: poll every live link and push its datagrams. Returns dead links.
    pub fn flush_all(&self) -> usize {
        let sessions: Vec<Arc<DataSession>> = {
            let mut v = self.data_sessions.lock();
            v.retain(|w| w.strong_count() > 1);
            v.iter().filter_map(|w| w.upgrade()).collect()
        };
        let mut dead = 0;
        for s in sessions {
            if !s.tick() {
                dead += 1;
                match &s.sink {
                    DataSink::Quic(c) => c.close(4u32.into(), b"link dead"),
                    DataSink::WebTransport(c) => c.close(4u32.into(), b"link dead"),
                    DataSink::Ws(_) => {}
                }
            }
        }
        dead
    }

    pub fn insert(&self, project: ProjectId, room: Room) -> Arc<Mutex<HostedRoom>> {
        let id = room.id();
        let name = room.cfg.name.clone();
        let h = Arc::new(Mutex::new(HostedRoom {
            room,
            sessions: HashMap::new(),
            project,
            sync: None,
            lockstep: None,
        }));
        self.rooms.insert(id, h.clone());
        self.by_name.insert((project, name), id);
        h
    }

    pub fn get(&self, id: RoomId) -> Option<Arc<Mutex<HostedRoom>>> {
        self.rooms.get(&id).map(|r| r.clone())
    }

    pub fn by_name(&self, project: ProjectId, name: &str) -> Option<Arc<Mutex<HostedRoom>>> {
        let id = *self.by_name.get(&(project, name.to_string()))?;
        self.get(id)
    }

    pub fn remove(&self, id: RoomId) -> Option<Arc<Mutex<HostedRoom>>> {
        let (_, h) = self.rooms.remove(&id)?;
        let (project, name) = {
            let g = h.lock();
            (g.project, g.room.cfg.name.clone())
        };
        self.by_name.remove(&(project, name));
        Some(h)
    }

    /// Per project: (rooms, online players, new bytes in, new bytes out) since the last call.
    pub fn usage(&self) -> HashMap<ProjectId, (u64, u64, u64, u64)> {
        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
        let mut out: HashMap<ProjectId, (u64, u64, u64, u64)> = HashMap::new();
        for r in self.rooms.iter() {
            let g = r.value().lock();
            let e = out.entry(g.project).or_default();
            e.0 += 1;
            e.1 += g.room.online_count() as u64;
            for s in g.sessions.values() {
                if let Some(d) = &s.data {
                    let st = d.link.lock().stats();
                    let din = st
                        .recv_bytes
                        .saturating_sub(d.metered_in.swap(st.recv_bytes, Ordering::Relaxed));
                    let dout = st
                        .sent_bytes
                        .saturating_sub(d.metered_out.swap(st.sent_bytes, Ordering::Relaxed));
                    e.2 += din;
                    e.3 += dout;
                }
            }
        }
        out
    }

    /// Rooms hosted here where `player_id` has a slot: (room id, room name, mode, actor, display name, online).
    pub fn find_player(
        &self,
        project: ProjectId,
        player_id: &str,
    ) -> Vec<(RoomId, String, net_common::RoomMode, u16, String, bool)> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for r in self.rooms.iter() {
            let g = r.value().lock();
            if g.project != project {
                continue;
            }
            for p in g.room.player_infos() {
                if p.player_id == player_id {
                    out.push((
                        *r.key(),
                        g.room.cfg.name.clone(),
                        g.room.cfg.mode,
                        p.actor.0,
                        p.name.clone(),
                        p.online,
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
        out
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.rooms.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.rooms.is_empty()
    }

    pub fn players(&self) -> usize {
        self.rooms
            .iter()
            .map(|r| r.lock().room.online_count() as usize)
            .sum()
    }

    pub fn all(&self) -> Vec<Arc<Mutex<HostedRoom>>> {
        self.rooms.iter().map(|r| r.clone()).collect()
    }

    pub fn listed(&self, project: ProjectId) -> Vec<net_rooms::protocol::RoomSummary> {
        self.rooms
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|r| {
                let g = r.lock();
                (g.project == project && g.room.is_listed()).then(|| g.room.summary())
            })
            .collect()
    }

    pub fn presence_enter(&self, project: ProjectId, player: &str) {
        *self
            .presence
            .entry((project, player.to_string()))
            .or_default() += 1;
    }

    pub fn presence_leave(&self, project: ProjectId, player: &str) {
        let key = (project, player.to_string());
        let gone = match self.presence.get_mut(&key) {
            Some(mut n) => {
                *n = n.saturating_sub(1);
                *n == 0
            }
            None => false,
        };
        if gone {
            self.presence.remove_if(&key, |_, n| *n == 0);
        }
    }

    /// Whether `player` has an authenticated control session on this node right now.
    pub fn is_online(&self, project: ProjectId, player: &str) -> bool {
        self.presence
            .get(&(project, player.to_string()))
            .is_some_and(|n| *n > 0)
    }

    pub fn subscribe_lobby(&self, project: ProjectId, tx: mpsc::Sender<ServerMsg>) {
        self.lobby.entry(project).or_default().push(tx);
    }

    pub fn unsubscribe_lobby(&self, project: ProjectId, tx: &mpsc::Sender<ServerMsg>) {
        if let Some(mut v) = self.lobby.get_mut(&project) {
            v.retain(|t| !t.same_channel(tx));
        }
    }

    pub fn notify_lobby(&self, project: ProjectId, msg: ServerMsg) {
        if let Some(mut v) = self.lobby.get_mut(&project) {
            v.retain(|t| !t.is_closed());
            for t in v.iter() {
                let _ = t.try_send(msg.clone());
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Delivers what the room logic produced.
pub fn dispatch(h: &HostedRoom, out: Vec<Outgoing>, metrics: &Metrics) {
    for o in out {
        match o {
            Outgoing::Control(actor, msg) => {
                if let Some(s) = h.sessions.get(&actor) {
                    let _ = s.control.try_send(msg);
                }
            }
            Outgoing::Data(actor, channel, frame) => {
                let Some(s) = h.sessions.get(&actor) else {
                    continue;
                };
                metrics
                    .events
                    .with_label_values(&[channel_name(channel)])
                    .inc();
                match &s.data {
                    Some(d) => d.send(channel, frame.encode()),
                    None => {
                        // No data path yet: fall back to the control channel.
                        use base64::Engine;
                        let _ = s.control.try_send(ServerMsg::Event {
                            code: frame.code,
                            from: frame.from,
                            data: base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&frame.payload),
                        });
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

pub fn channel_name(c: Channel) -> &'static str {
    match c {
        Channel::UnreliableSequenced => "unreliable_sequenced",
        Channel::ReliableOrdered => "reliable_ordered",
        Channel::ReliableUnordered => "reliable_unordered",
    }
}

/// Routes one data-path frame from `actor` through the room.
pub fn handle_data_frame(
    h: &mut HostedRoom,
    actor: ActorId,
    channel: Channel,
    payload: Bytes,
    metrics: &Metrics,
) -> Result<()> {
    // Simulation frames travel on any channel (inputs unreliable, checkpoint uploads
    // reliable); unknown kinds fall through to relay events.
    if let Some(sy) = h.sync.as_mut() {
        if sy.handle(actor, payload.clone()) {
            h.room.count_input(actor, payload.len(), Instant::now());
            return Ok(());
        }
    }
    if let Some(ls) = h.lockstep.as_mut() {
        if ls.handle(actor, payload.clone()) {
            h.room.count_input(actor, payload.len(), Instant::now());
            return Ok(());
        }
    }
    let frame = EventFrame::decode(payload).map_err(|e| NetError::Invalid(e.to_string()))?;
    let out = h
        .room
        .raise_event(actor, frame, channel, Instant::now())
        .map_err(|e| NetError::Invalid(e.to_string()))?;
    dispatch(h, out, metrics);
    Ok(())
}

`crates/net-api/src/janitor.rs`:

```rs
//! Hourly Postgres janitor: deletes closed rooms, audit and usage rows past `[retention]`.
//! Every node runs it; the deletes are idempotent, so overlap between nodes is harmless.

use crate::state::Shared;
use net_db::queries;
use std::time::Duration;

const EVERY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3600);

pub async fn run(st: Shared) {
    let mut iv = tokio::time::interval(EVERY);
    iv.set_missed_tick_behavior(tokio::time::MissedTickBehavior::Delay);
    loop {
        iv.tick().await;
        let jitter = std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| u64::from(d.subsec_nanos()) % 5_000)
            .unwrap_or(0);
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(jitter)).await;
        let r = &st.cfg.retention;
        for (what, res) in [
            (
                "rooms",
                queries::purge_closed_rooms(&st.pool, r.closed_rooms_days).await,
            ),
            ("audit", queries::purge_audit(&st.pool, r.audit_days).await),
            ("usage", queries::purge_usage(&st.pool, r.usage_days).await),
            ("bans", queries::purge_expired_bans(&st.pool).await),
            (
                "webhook_deliveries",
                queries::purge_webhook_deliveries(&st.pool, r.webhook_deliveries_days).await,
            ),
            (
                "operator_webhook_deliveries",
                queries::purge_operator_webhook_deliveries(&st.pool, r.webhook_deliveries_days)
                    .await,
            ),
        ] {
            match res {
                Ok(0) => {}
                Ok(n) => tracing::info!(table = what, deleted = n, "janitor"),
                Err(e) => tracing::warn!(table = what, error = %e, "janitor"),
            }
        }
    }
}
