```rs
#[test]
fn control_plane_json_survives_garbage() {
    let mut r = rng(31);
    let valid = [
        r#"{"t":"auth","grant":"abc"}"#,
        r#"{"t":"create","name":"arena","mode":"sync","max_players":8,"props":{"lobby":"ranked","tick_hz":30},"lobby_props":["lobby"]}"#,
        r#"{"t":"join","name":"arena","player_props":{"skin":1}}"#,
        r#"{"t":"find_friends","players":["ann","bob"]}"#,
        r#"{"t":"stats"}"#,
        r#"{"t":"set_player_props","props":{"ready":true},"expected":{"ready":false}}"#,
        r#"{"t":"ping","ts":1}"#,
    ];
    let alphabet: &[u8] = b"{}[]:,\"tauthcreatejoinpropsnamemode0123456789.-eE nulltruefalse";
    for i in 0..20_000usize {
        let v = valid[i % valid.len()].as_bytes();
        let _ = serde_json::from_slice::<ClientMsg>(&mutate(&mut r, v));
        let n = (r() as usize) % 100;
        let t: Vec<u8> = (0..n)
            .map(|_| alphabet[(r() as usize) % alphabet.len()])
            .collect();
        let _ = serde_json::from_slice::<ClientMsg>(&t);
        let _ = serde_json::from_slice::<ClientMsg>(&garbage(&mut r, 60));
    }
    let deep = format!(
        "{{\"t\":\"create\",\"props\":{{\"a\":{}1{}}}}}",
        "[".repeat(2000),
        "]".repeat(2000)
    );
    assert!(
        serde_json::from_str::<ClientMsg>(&deep).is_err(),
        "nesting beyond serde's recursion limit is rejected, not a stack overflow"
    );
    for m in valid {
        serde_json::from_str::<ClientMsg>(m).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{m}: {e}"));
    }
}
```

```rs
use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;

/// Operator token check; an empty configured token disables operator endpoints.
pub fn admin_token_ok(configured: &str, presented: &str) -> bool {
    !configured.is_empty()
        && configured.len() == presented.len()
        && configured
            .as_bytes()
            .ct_eq(presented.as_bytes())
            .unwrap_u8()
            == 1
}

#[cfg(test)]

        assert!(!super::admin_token_ok("", ""));
        assert!(super::admin_token_ok("abc", "abc"));
        assert!(!super::admin_token_ok("abc", "abd"));
    }
}
```

`crates/net-auth/src/api_key.rs`:

```rs
//! `an_<prefix8>_<secret>`: the prefix is stored in clear for display, the whole key only as
//! SHA-256. Keys are shown once at creation.

use base64::Engine;
use rand::Rng;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Scope {
    /// Issue join grants, create/close rooms, read room lists.
    Rooms,
    /// Read usage and audit.
    Read,
    /// Manage keys, webhooks, schemas.
    Admin,
}

impl Scope {
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Scope::Rooms => "rooms",
            Scope::Read => "read",
            Scope::Admin => "admin",
        }
    }
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match s {
            "rooms" => Some(Scope::Rooms),
            "read" => Some(Scope::Read),
            "admin" => Some(Scope::Admin),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ApiKeyMaterial {
    pub plaintext: String,
    pub prefix: String,
    pub hash: String,
}

impl ApiKeyMaterial {
    pub fn generate() -> Self {
        let mut raw = [0u8; 32];
        rand::rng().fill_bytes(&mut raw);
        let secret = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(raw);
        let prefix = secret[..8].to_string();
        let plaintext = format!("an_{prefix}_{}", &secret[8..]);
        let hash = hash_key(&plaintext);
        Self {
            plaintext,
            prefix,
            hash,
        }
    }
}

pub fn hash_key(plaintext: &str) -> String {
    hex::encode(Sha256::digest(plaintext.as_bytes()))
}

/// Cheap syntactic check before hitting the database.
pub fn looks_like_key(s: &str) -> bool {
    s.len() > 12 && s.starts_with("an_") && s.is_ascii()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn generate_and_hash() {
        let k = ApiKeyMaterial::generate();
        assert!(looks_like_key(&k.plaintext));
        assert_eq!(k.hash, hash_key(&k.plaintext));
        assert_eq!(k.hash.len(), 64);
        assert_ne!(k.hash, ApiKeyMaterial::generate().hash);
    }
}
```

`crates/net-auth/src/grant.rs`:

```rs
//! Join grants: the developer's backend asks the control plane for a short-lived token
//! naming the player and what they may do; the client presents it over the control channel.

use chrono::Utc;
use jsonwebtoken::{Algorithm, DecodingKey, EncodingKey, Header, Validation};
use net_common::{NetError, ProjectId, Result};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
pub struct GrantClaims {
    /// Player id chosen by the developer (stable per user).
    pub sub: String,
    /// Project id.
    pub pid: String,
    /// Display name shown to other players.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub name: String,
    /// If set, the grant only admits to this room name.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub room: Option<String>,
    /// `join`, `create`, `master`.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub scopes: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub meta: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    pub exp: i64,
    pub iat: i64,
    pub jti: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Grant {
    pub player_id: String,
    pub project: ProjectId,
    pub name: String,
    pub room: Option<String>,
    pub scopes: Vec<String>,
    pub meta: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    pub jti: String,
    pub exp: i64,
}

impl Grant {
    pub fn can(&self, scope: &str) -> bool {
        self.scopes.iter().any(|s| s == scope)
    }
}

/// Largest `meta` payload a grant may carry (the grant travels in the first WS message).
pub const MAX_META_BYTES: usize = 1024;
pub const KNOWN_SCOPES: &[&str] = &["join", "create", "master", "spectate"];

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct GrantSigner {
    enc: EncodingKey,
    dec: DecodingKey,
    /// Decoding key of the secret being rotated out; accepted until the operator drops it.
    prev: Option<DecodingKey>,
    ttl_secs: i64,
}

impl GrantSigner {
    pub fn new(secret: &str, ttl_secs: u64) -> Self {
        Self::with_previous(secret, None, ttl_secs)
    }

    pub fn with_previous(secret: &str, previous: Option<&str>, ttl_secs: u64) -> Self {
        Self {
            enc: EncodingKey::from_secret(secret.as_bytes()),
            dec: DecodingKey::from_secret(secret.as_bytes()),
            prev: previous.map(|p| DecodingKey::from_secret(p.as_bytes())),
            ttl_secs: ttl_secs as i64,
        }
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn issue(
        &self,
        project: ProjectId,
        player_id: &str,
        name: &str,
        room: Option<&str>,
        scopes: &[&str],
        meta: Option<serde_json::Value>,
        ttl_override: Option<u64>,
    ) -> Result<(String, GrantClaims)> {
        if player_id.is_empty() || player_id.len() > 128 {
            return Err(NetError::Invalid("player_id must be 1..=128 chars".into()));
        }
        if player_id.chars().any(char::is_control) {
            return Err(NetError::Invalid("player_id has control characters".into()));
        }
        if let Some(m) = &meta {
            let n = serde_json::to_vec(m).map(|v| v.len()).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
            if n > MAX_META_BYTES {
                return Err(NetError::Invalid(format!(
                    "meta must serialize to <= {MAX_META_BYTES} bytes"
                )));
            }
        }
        for s in scopes {
            if !KNOWN_SCOPES.contains(s) {
                return Err(NetError::Invalid(format!("unknown scope {s}")));
            }
        }
        let now = Utc::now().timestamp();
        let ttl = ttl_override
            .map(|t| (t as i64).min(self.ttl_secs))
            .unwrap_or(self.ttl_secs);
        let claims = GrantClaims {
            sub: player_id.to_string(),
            pid: project.to_string(),
            name: name.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control()).take(64).collect(),
            room: room.map(|r| r.to_string()),
            scopes: scopes.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),
            meta,
            exp: now + ttl,
            iat: now,
            jti: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
        };
        let token = jsonwebtoken::encode(&Header::new(Algorithm::HS256), &claims, &self.enc)
            .map_err(|e| NetError::Internal(format!("sign grant: {e}")))?;
        Ok((token, claims))
    }

    pub fn verify(&self, token: &str) -> Result<Grant> {
        let mut v = Validation::new(Algorithm::HS256);
        v.leeway = 5;
        v.validate_exp = true;
        v.required_spec_claims.clear();
        let data = match jsonwebtoken::decode::<GrantClaims>(token, &self.dec, &v) {
            Ok(d) => d,
            Err(e) if matches!(e.kind(), jsonwebtoken::errors::ErrorKind::InvalidSignature) => {
                match &self.prev {
                    Some(prev) => jsonwebtoken::decode::<GrantClaims>(token, prev, &v)
                        .map_err(|e| NetError::Unauthorized(format!("grant: {e}")))?,
                    None => return Err(NetError::Unauthorized(format!("grant: {e}"))),
                }
            }
            Err(e) => return Err(NetError::Unauthorized(format!("grant: {e}"))),
        };
        let c = data.claims;
        let project = c
            .pid
            .parse::<ProjectId>()
            .map_err(|_| NetError::Unauthorized("grant: bad project id".into()))?;
        Ok(Grant {
            player_id: c.sub,
            project,
            name: c.name,
            room: c.room,
            scopes: c.scopes,
            meta: c.meta,
            jti: c.jti,
            exp: c.exp,
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn rotation_accepts_previous_secret_only_while_configured() {
        let old = GrantSigner::new("old-secret", 60);
        let (tok, _) = old
            .issue(ProjectId::new(), "p1", "Ann", None, &["join"], None, None)
            .unwrap();
        let rotated = GrantSigner::with_previous("new-secret", Some("old-secret"), 60);
        assert_eq!(rotated.verify(&tok).unwrap().player_id, "p1");
        let (fresh, _) = rotated
            .issue(ProjectId::new(), "p2", "Bob", None, &["join"], None, None)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rotated.verify(&fresh).unwrap().player_id, "p2");
        assert!(old.verify(&fresh).is_err());
        let dropped = GrantSigner::new("new-secret", 60);
        assert!(dropped.verify(&tok).is_err());
        let wrong = GrantSigner::with_previous("new-secret", Some("other"), 60);
        assert!(wrong.verify(&tok).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn issue_verify() {
        let s = GrantSigner::new("s3cret", 60);
        let p = ProjectId::new();
        let (tok, _) = s
            .issue(
                p,
                "player-1",
                "Ann",
                Some("lobby"),
                &["join", "create"],
                None,
                None,
            )
            .unwrap();
        let g = s.verify(&tok).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(g.player_id, "player-1");
        assert_eq!(g.project, p);
        assert_eq!(g.room.as_deref(), Some("lobby"));
        assert!(g.can("join"));
        assert!(!g.can("master"));
        assert!(GrantSigner::new("other", 60).verify(&tok).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn ttl_is_capped() {
        let s = GrantSigner::new("s3cret", 60);
        let (_, c) = s
            .issue(ProjectId::new(), "p", "", None, &[], None, Some(10_000))
            .unwrap();
        assert!(c.exp - c.iat <= 60);
    }
}
```

```rs
//! `aurix-net`: command line over the REST API. Developer calls use an API key
//! (`--api-key` / `NET_API_KEY`), operator calls use `--operator-token` / `NET_OPERATOR_TOKEN`.

use clap::{Parser, Subcommand};
use serde_json::{json, Value};

#[derive(Parser)]
#[command(name = "aurix-net", version, about = "Aurix Net command line")]
struct Cli {
    #[arg(long, env = "NET_HTTP", default_value = "http://127.0.0.1:8090")]
    http: String,
    #[arg(long, env = "NET_API_KEY")]
    api_key: Option<String>,
    #[arg(long, env = "NET_OPERATOR_TOKEN")]
    operator_token: Option<String>,
    #[command(subcommand)]
    cmd: Cmd,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
enum Cmd {
    /// Node health
    Health,
    /// Regions with live nodes
    Regions,
    /// Operator: create a project (prints the first API key once)
    ProjectCreate {
        name: String,
        #[arg(long, default_value = "indie")]
        plan: String,
    },
    /// Operator: list projects
    Projects,
    /// Operator: nodes
    Nodes,
    /// Create an API key (admin scope on the current key)
    KeyCreate {
        #[arg(long, default_value = "cli")]
        name: String,
        #[arg(long, value_delimiter = ',', default_value = "read,rooms,grants")]
        scopes: Vec<String>,
    },
    Keys,
    /// Issue a join grant for a player
    Grant {
        player_id: String,
        #[arg(long)]
        name: Option<String>,
        #[arg(long)]
        room: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Open rooms
    Rooms,
    Room {
        id: String,
    },
    RoomClose {
        id: String,
    },
    /// Download a lockstep replay (JSON) of a closed room
    Replay {
        id: String,
        #[arg(short, long)]
        out: Option<String>,
    },
    /// File a matchmaking ticket and wait for a match
    Match {
        player_id: String,
        #[arg(long, default_value = "relay")]
        mode: String,
        #[arg(long, default_value_t = 2)]
        max_players: u16,
        #[arg(long, default_value_t = 2)]
        min_players: u16,
        #[arg(long, default_value_t = 15)]
        max_wait_secs: u64,
        /// Player attributes as JSON (`{"rank": 1450}`) other tickets may filter on
        #[arg(long)]
        attrs: Option<String>,
        /// SQL-like condition on the other players' attrs (`rank >= 1300 AND rank <= 1600`)
        #[arg(long)]
        filter: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Usage (node-hours, events, bytes)
    Usage,
    Webhooks,
    WebhookCreate {
        url: String,
        #[arg(long, value_delimiter = ',')]
        events: Vec<String>,
    },
    /// List the project's server-side game modules (WASM logic for sync rooms).
    Modules,
    /// Upload or replace a game module (.wasm binary or .wat text); rooms use it via props.logic.
    ModulePut {
        name: String,
        file: std::path::PathBuf,
    },
    ModuleDelete {
        name: String,
    },
}

struct Api {
    http: reqwest::Client,
    base: String,
    bearer: Option<String>,
}

impl Api {
    async fn call(
        &self,
        method: reqwest::Method,
        path: &str,
        body: Option<Value>,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
        let mut r = self.http.request(method, format!("{}{}", self.base, path));
        if let Some(b) = &self.bearer {
            r = r.bearer_auth(b);
        }
        if let Some(b) = body {
            r = r.json(&b);
        }
        let resp = r.send().await?;
        let status = resp.status();
        let text = resp.text().await?;
        if !status.is_success() {
            anyhow::bail!("{status}: {text}");
        }
        if text.is_empty() {
            return Ok(json!({"ok": true}));
        }
        Ok(serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap_or(Value::String(text)))
    }

    async fn call_raw(
        &self,
        method: reqwest::Method,
        path: &str,
        body: Vec<u8>,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
        let mut r = self
            .http
            .request(method, format!("{}{}", self.base, path))
            .header("content-type", "application/octet-stream")
            .body(body);
        if let Some(b) = &self.bearer {
            r = r.bearer_auth(b);
        }
        let resp = r.send().await?;
        let status = resp.status();
        let text = resp.text().await?;
        if !status.is_success() {
            anyhow::bail!("{status}: {text}");
        }
        Ok(serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap_or(Value::String(text)))
    }
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let cli = Cli::parse();
    const GET: reqwest::Method = reqwest::Method::GET;
    const POST: reqwest::Method = reqwest::Method::POST;
    const DELETE: reqwest::Method = reqwest::Method::DELETE;
    let dev = Api {
        http: reqwest::Client::new(),
        base: cli.http.clone(),
        bearer: cli.api_key.clone(),
    };
    let op = Api {
        http: reqwest::Client::new(),
        base: cli.http.clone(),
        bearer: cli.operator_token.clone(),
    };
    let need = |v: &Option<String>, what: &str| -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        if v.is_none() {
            anyhow::bail!("{what} required");
        }
        Ok(())
    };
    let out = match cli.cmd {
        Cmd::Health => dev.call(GET, "/healthz", None).await?,
        Cmd::Regions => dev.call(GET, "/v1/regions", None).await?,
        Cmd::ProjectCreate { name, plan } => {
            need(&cli.operator_token, "--operator-token")?;
            op.call(
                POST,
                "/v1/operator/projects",
                Some(json!({"name": name, "plan": plan})),
            )
            .await?
        }
        Cmd::Projects => {
            need(&cli.operator_token, "--operator-token")?;
            op.call(GET, "/v1/operator/projects", None).await?
        }
        Cmd::Nodes => {
            need(&cli.operator_token, "--operator-token")?;
            op.call(GET, "/v1/operator/nodes", None).await?
        }
        Cmd::KeyCreate { name, scopes } => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            dev.call(
                POST,
                "/v1/keys",
                Some(json!({"name": name, "scopes": scopes})),
            )
            .await?
        }
        Cmd::Keys => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            dev.call(GET, "/v1/keys", None).await?
        }
        Cmd::Grant {
            player_id,
            name,
            room,
        } => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            dev.call(POST, "/v1/grants", Some(json!({"player_id": player_id, "name": name.unwrap_or_else(|| player_id_name(&player_id)), "room": room}))).await?
        }
        Cmd::Rooms => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            dev.call(GET, "/v1/rooms", None).await?
        }
        Cmd::Room { id } => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            dev.call(GET, &format!("/v1/rooms/{id}"), None).await?
        }
        Cmd::RoomClose { id } => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            dev.call(DELETE, &format!("/v1/rooms/{id}"), None).await?
        }
        Cmd::Replay { id, out } => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            let v = dev
                .call(GET, &format!("/v1/rooms/{id}/replay"), None)
                .await?;
            if let Some(path) = out {
                std::fs::write(&path, serde_json::to_vec(&v)?)?;
                json!({"written": path, "ticks": v["inputs"].as_array().map(|a| a.len()).unwrap_or(0)})
            } else {
                v
            }
        }
        Cmd::Match {
            player_id,
            mode,
            max_players,
            min_players,
            max_wait_secs,
            attrs,
            filter,
        } => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            let attrs: serde_json::Value = match attrs {
                Some(a) => serde_json::from_str(&a).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("--attrs: {e}"))?,
                None => json!({}),
            };
            let t = dev
                .call(POST, "/v1/matchmaking/tickets", Some(json!({"player_id": player_id, "mode": mode, "max_players": max_players, "min_players": min_players, "max_wait_secs": max_wait_secs, "attrs": attrs, "filter": filter})))
                .await?;
            let id = t["ticket"].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_string();
            loop {
                let s = dev
                    .call(GET, &format!("/v1/matchmaking/tickets/{id}"), None)
                    .await?;
                if s["state"]["state"] != "searching" {
                    break s;
                }
                eprintln!("searching... waiting={}", s["state"]["waiting"]);
                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(500)).await;
            }
        }
        Cmd::Usage => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            dev.call(GET, "/v1/usage", None).await?
        }
        Cmd::Webhooks => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            dev.call(GET, "/v1/webhooks", None).await?
        }
        Cmd::WebhookCreate { url, events } => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            dev.call(
                POST,
                "/v1/webhooks",
                Some(json!({"url": url, "events": events})),
            )
            .await?
        }
        Cmd::Modules => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            dev.call(GET, "/v1/modules", None).await?
        }
        Cmd::ModulePut { name, file } => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            let bytes = std::fs::read(&file)?;
            dev.call_raw(reqwest::Method::PUT, &format!("/v1/modules/{name}"), bytes)
                .await?
        }
        Cmd::ModuleDelete { name } => {
            need(&cli.api_key, "--api-key")?;
            dev.call(
                reqwest::Method::DELETE,
                &format!("/v1/modules/{name}"),
                None,
            )
            .await?
        }
    };
    println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out)?);
    Ok(())
}

fn player_id_name(p: &str) -> String {
    p.chars().take(32).collect()
}
```

```rs
//! Joins a room by name through any node of the region; `connect_and_join` follows the
//! `room_elsewhere:<url>` redirect to the node hosting it.
//! Usage: follow <http_url> <api_key> <room>
use net_client::{Client, Options};
use net_rooms::protocol::ClientMsg;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let a: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let (http, key, room) = (&a[1], &a[2], &a[3]);
    let grant: serde_json::Value = reqwest::Client::new()
        .post(format!("{http}/v1/grants"))
        .bearer_auth(key)
        .json(&serde_json::json!({"player_id": "follow-1", "name": "follow"}))
        .send()
        .await?
        .error_for_status()?
        .json()
        .await?;
    let msg: ClientMsg = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({
        "t": "join_or_create", "name": room, "mode": "relay", "max_players": 8, "props": {}
    }))?;
    let (c, j) = Client::connect_and_join(
        http,
        grant["grant"].as_str().unwrap(),
        Options::default(),
        msg,
    )
    .await?;
    println!(
        "joined room={} actor={:?} via data host={}:{}",
        j.name, j.actor, j.data.host, j.data.port
    );
    drop(c);
    Ok(())
}
```

`crates/net-client/examples/rehost.rs`:

```rs
//! Live check of `Client::rejoin`: joins a lockstep room, waits for `left{reason:"rehost"}`
//! (node shutting down), rejoins through the fallback URL and prints what it sees.
//! Usage: rehost <http_url> <grant> <room_name> <fallback_url>
use net_client::{Client, Event, Options};
use net_rooms::protocol::{ClientMsg, ServerMsg};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let a: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    let (url, grant, room, fallback) = (&a[1], &a[2], &a[3], &a[4]);
    let join = ClientMsg::JoinOrCreate {
        name: room.clone(),
        mode: net_common::types::RoomMode::Lockstep,
        max_players: Some(4),
        props: serde_json::from_str(r#"{"tick_hz":60}"#)?,
        lobby_props: vec![],
        region: None,
        player_props: Default::default(),
        reserved: Vec::new(),
    };
    let (mut c, j) = Client::connect_and_join(url, grant, Options::default(), join).await?;
    println!("joined room={} actor={} on {url}", j.name, j.actor.0);
    let mut bundles = 0u32;
    loop {
        match c.next_event().await {
            Some(Event::Control(ServerMsg::Left { reason })) => {
                println!("left: {reason} after {bundles} bundles");
                if reason != "rehost" {
                    anyhow::bail!("unexpected leave");
                }
                let (mut c2, j2) = c.rejoin(&[fallback.as_str()]).await?;
                println!(
                    "rejoined room={} actor={} (same actor: {})",
                    j2.name,
                    j2.actor.0,
                    j2.actor == j.actor
                );
                let mut n = 0;
                while n < 60 {
                    match c2.next_event().await {
                        Some(Event::Data { .. }) => n += 1,
                        Some(Event::Closed(r)) => anyhow::bail!("closed after rejoin: {r}"),
                        None => anyhow::bail!("stream ended after rejoin"),
                        _ => {}
                    }
                }
                println!("REHOST_OK: {n} data frames after rejoin");
                return Ok(());
            }
            Some(Event::Data { .. }) => bundles += 1,
            Some(Event::Closed(r)) => anyhow::bail!("closed: {r}"),
            None => anyhow::bail!("stream ended"),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/net-client/examples/relay_echo.rs`:

```rs
//! Two clients join one relay room; A sends an event, B receives it.
//! `NET_API_KEY=an_... cargo run -p net-client --example relay_echo`

use bytes::Bytes;
use net_client::protocol::{ClientMsg, ServerMsg};
use net_client::{issue_grant, Client, Event, EventFrame, EventTarget, Options};
use net_common::RoomMode;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let http = std::env::var("NET_HTTP").unwrap_or_else(|_| "http://127.0.0.1:8090".into());
    let key = std::env::var("NET_API_KEY")?;
    let room = format!("echo-{}", std::process::id());
    let join = |name: &str| ClientMsg::JoinOrCreate {
        name: name.to_string(),
        mode: RoomMode::Relay,
        max_players: Some(4),
        props: Default::default(),
        lobby_props: vec![],
        region: None,
        player_props: Default::default(),
        reserved: Vec::new(),
    };

    let ga = issue_grant(&http, &key, "alice", "Alice").await?;
    let gb = issue_grant(&http, &key, "bob", "Bob").await?;
    let mut a = Client::connect(&http, &ga, Options::default()).await?;
    let mut b = Client::connect(
        &http,
        &gb,
        Options {
            tunnel: true,
            ..Default::default()
        },
    )
    .await?;
    let ja = a.join(join(&room)).await?;
    let jb = b.join(join(&room)).await?;
    println!(
        "alice actor={} (quic), bob actor={} (ws tunnel), room={}",
        ja.actor.0, jb.actor.0, ja.name
    );

    // A: reliable hello, then 10 unreliable ticks
    a.send_event(1, EventTarget::Others, Bytes::from_static(b"hello"), true)?;
    for i in 0..10u8 {
        a.send_event(2, EventTarget::Others, Bytes::from(vec![i]), false)?;
        a.flush();
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(16)).await;
    }

    let mut got_hello = false;
    let mut ticks = 0;
    let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(3);
    while let Ok(Some(ev)) = tokio::time::timeout_at(deadline, b.next_event()).await {
        match ev {
            Event::Data { payload, .. } => {
                let f = EventFrame::decode(payload)?;
                match f.code {
                    1 => got_hello = f.payload.as_ref() == b"hello" && f.from == ja.actor,
                    2 => ticks += 1,
                    _ => {}
                }
                if got_hello && ticks == 10 {
                    break;
                }
            }
            Event::Control(ServerMsg::PlayerJoined { player }) => {
                println!("bob sees joined: {}", player.name)
            }
            Event::Closed(r) => return Err(format!("closed: {r}").into()),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    println!(
        "bob got hello={got_hello} ticks={ticks}/10 stats={:?}",
        b.link_stats()
    );
    a.leave().await?;
    assert!(got_hello && ticks == 10, "echo failed");
    Ok(())
}
```

`crates/net-client/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Rust client for Aurix Net: control channel over WebSocket, data path over QUIC (pinned
//! certificate) or the WebSocket tunnel, with the same `Link` channels the server uses.
//! Engine SDKs and the C ABI are thin layers over this crate.

pub mod lockstep;
pub mod rollback;

use base64::Engine;
use bytes::Bytes;
use futures::{SinkExt, StreamExt};
use net_common::{Channel, RoomMode};
use net_rooms::protocol::{ClientMsg, DataEndpoint, ServerMsg};
use net_transport::{quic, Link};
use parking_lot::Mutex;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use tokio::sync::mpsc;
use tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Message;

pub use net_common;
pub use net_rooms::event::{CacheOp, EventFrame, EventTarget};
pub use net_rooms::protocol;

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum ClientError {
    #[error("http: {0}")]
    Http(String),
    #[error("websocket: {0}")]
    Ws(String),
    #[error("server: {code}: {message}")]
    Server { code: String, message: String },
    #[error("data path: {0}")]
    Data(String),
    #[error("disconnected")]
    Disconnected,
    #[error("timeout")]
    Timeout,
}

pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, ClientError>;

/// Issues a join grant through the developer's API key. Game servers / backends only: the key
/// must never ship inside a game client.
pub async fn issue_grant(
    http_url: &str,
    api_key: &str,
    player_id: &str,
    name: &str,
) -> Result<String> {
    let v: serde_json::Value = reqwest::Client::new()
        .post(format!("{http_url}/v1/grants"))
        .bearer_auth(api_key)
        .json(&serde_json::json!({ "player_id": player_id, "name": name }))
        .send()
        .await
        .map_err(|e| ClientError::Http(e.to_string()))?
        .error_for_status()
        .map_err(|e| ClientError::Http(e.to_string()))?
        .json()
        .await
        .map_err(|e| ClientError::Http(e.to_string()))?;
    v["grant"]
        .as_str()
        .map(str::to_string)
        .ok_or_else(|| ClientError::Http("no grant in response".into()))
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Options {
    /// Force the WebSocket tunnel instead of QUIC.
    pub tunnel: bool,
    pub connect_timeout: Duration,
    /// How often the link timer runs (acks, retransmits, batches).
    pub tick: Duration,
}

impl Default for Options {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            tunnel: false,
            connect_timeout: Duration::from_secs(10),
            tick: Duration::from_millis(5),
        }
    }
}

/// Everything the game sees from the server.
#[derive(Debug)]
#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]
pub enum Event {
    /// Any control message (Joined, PlayerJoined, Event via control fallback, Desync, ...).
    Control(ServerMsg),
    /// A data-path message on `channel` (relay event frame, sync delta, lockstep bundle).
    Data {
        channel: Channel,
        tick: u16,
        payload: Bytes,
    },
    /// Data path became ready (first ack from the server).
    DataReady,
    Closed(String),
}

enum Sink {
    Quic(quinn::Connection),
    Ws(mpsc::Sender<Message>),
}

struct DataPath {
    link: Mutex<Link>,
    sink: Sink,
}

impl DataPath {
    fn flush(&self) {
        let out: Vec<Bytes> = {
            let mut l = self.link.lock();
            std::iter::from_fn(|| l.next_outgoing()).collect()
        };
        for d in out {
            match &self.sink {
                Sink::Quic(c) => {
                    let _ = c.send_datagram(d);
                }
                Sink::Ws(tx) => {
                    let _ = tx.try_send(Message::Binary(d));
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

pub struct Client {
    ctl: mpsc::Sender<Message>,
    events: mpsc::Receiver<Event>,
    events_tx: mpsc::Sender<Event>,
    data: Option<Arc<DataPath>>,
    opts: Options,
    pub joined: Option<Joined>,
    tasks: Vec<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>,
    tunnel_slot: Option<Arc<Mutex<Option<Arc<DataPath>>>>>,
    /// What `rejoin` needs after a rehost: the URL given to `connect`, the grant, the last join.
    entry_url: String,
    grant: String,
    last_join: Option<ClientMsg>,
}

/// Room facts from the `joined` message.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Joined {
    pub room: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub mode: RoomMode,
    pub actor: net_common::ActorId,
    pub master: net_common::ActorId,
    pub tick_hz: Option<u16>,
    pub schema_hash: Option<String>,
    pub data: DataEndpoint,
}

impl Client {
    /// Opens the control channel and authenticates with a grant.
    pub async fn connect(http_url: &str, grant: &str, opts: Options) -> Result<Client> {
        let ws_url = http_url.replacen("http", "ws", 1) + "/ws";
        let (ws, _) = tokio::time::timeout(
            opts.connect_timeout,
            tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(&ws_url),
        )
        .await
        .map_err(|_| ClientError::Timeout)?
        .map_err(|e| ClientError::Ws(e.to_string()))?;
        let (mut tx, mut rx) = ws.split();
        let (ctl, mut ctl_rx) = mpsc::channel::<Message>(256);
        let (events_tx, events) = mpsc::channel::<Event>(4096);
        let writer = tokio::spawn(async move {
            while let Some(m) = ctl_rx.recv().await {
                if tx.send(m).await.is_err() {
                    break;
                }
            }
        });
        let mut c = Client {
            ctl,
            events,
            events_tx: events_tx.clone(),
            data: None,
            opts,
            joined: None,
            tasks: vec![writer],
            tunnel_slot: None,
            entry_url: http_url.to_string(),
            grant: grant.to_string(),
            last_join: None,
        };
        // Reader: text -> Control events, binary -> tunnel datagrams (routed via data path if any).
        let tunnel_in: Arc<Mutex<Option<Arc<DataPath>>>> = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));
        let tunnel_slot = tunnel_in.clone();
        let reader = tokio::spawn(async move {
            while let Some(m) = rx.next().await {
                match m {
                    Ok(Message::Text(t)) => match serde_json::from_str::<ServerMsg>(&t) {
                        Ok(msg) => {
                            if events_tx.send(Event::Control(msg)).await.is_err() {
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                        Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, "bad control message"),
                    },
                    Ok(Message::Binary(b)) => {
                        let dp = tunnel_slot.lock().clone();
                        if let Some(dp) = dp {
                            deliver(&dp, b, &events_tx).await;
                        }
                    }
                    Ok(Message::Close(_)) | Err(_) => {
                        let _ = events_tx
                            .send(Event::Closed("control channel closed".into()))
                            .await;
                        break;
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
        });
        c.tasks.push(reader);
        c.tunnel_slot = Some(tunnel_in);
        c.send(ClientMsg::Auth {
            grant: grant.to_string(),
        })
        .await?;
        // wait for Authed (or Error)
        loop {
            match c.next_event().await {
                Some(Event::Control(ServerMsg::Authed { .. })) => break,
                Some(Event::Control(ServerMsg::Hello { .. })) => continue,
                Some(Event::Control(ServerMsg::Error { code, message })) => {
                    return Err(ClientError::Server { code, message })
                }
                Some(Event::Closed(_)) | None => return Err(ClientError::Disconnected),
                _ => continue,
            }
        }
        Ok(c)
    }

    /// Sends a control message.
    pub async fn send(&self, msg: ClientMsg) -> Result<()> {
        let txt = serde_json::to_string(&msg).map_err(|e| ClientError::Ws(e.to_string()))?;
        self.ctl
            .send(Message::Text(txt.into()))
            .await
            .map_err(|_| ClientError::Disconnected)
    }

    /// `connect` + `join`, following one `room_elsewhere:<url>` redirect: rooms are pinned to
    /// the node that hosts them, so a join sent to another node of the region answers with
    /// the hosting node's URL and the client reconnects there with the same grant.
    pub async fn connect_and_join(
        http_url: &str,
        grant: &str,
        opts: Options,
        msg: ClientMsg,
    ) -> Result<(Client, Joined)> {
        let mut c = Client::connect(http_url, grant, opts.clone()).await?;
        match c.join(msg.clone()).await {
            Ok(j) => Ok((c, j)),
            Err(ClientError::Server { code, message })
                if code == "conflict" && message.contains("room_elsewhere:") =>
            {
                let url = message
                    .split("room_elsewhere:")
                    .nth(1)
                    .unwrap_or_default()
                    .trim()
                    .to_string();
                drop(c);
                let mut c = Client::connect(&url, grant, opts).await?;
                let j = c.join(msg).await?;
                Ok((c, j))
            }
            Err(e) => Err(e),
        }
    }

    /// Joins (or creates) a room and opens the data path. Returns when the data path is ready.
    /// After `left{reason:"rehost"}` (the node shut down and handed the room to another node):
    /// a fresh client in the same room with the same grant, trying the entry URL then
    /// `fallback_urls` (other nodes / the region URL).
    pub async fn rejoin(self, fallback_urls: &[&str]) -> Result<(Client, Joined)> {
        let msg = match self.last_join.clone() {
            Some(ClientMsg::JoinOrCreate {
                name, player_props, ..
            }) => ClientMsg::Join {
                name,
                player_props,
                rejoin_actor: None,
                schema_hash: None,
                spectator: false,
            },
            Some(m) => m,
            None => return Err(ClientError::Disconnected),
        };
        let (entry, grant, opts) = (
            self.entry_url.clone(),
            self.grant.clone(),
            self.opts.clone(),
        );
        drop(self);
        let mut last = ClientError::Disconnected;
        for url in std::iter::once(entry.as_str()).chain(fallback_urls.iter().copied()) {
            match Client::connect_and_join(url, &grant, opts.clone(), msg.clone()).await {
                Ok(r) => return Ok(r),
                Err(e) => last = e,
            }
        }
        Err(last)
    }

    pub async fn join(&mut self, msg: ClientMsg) -> Result<Joined> {
        self.last_join = Some(msg.clone());
        self.send(msg).await?;
        let joined = loop {
            match self.next_event().await {
                Some(Event::Control(ServerMsg::Joined {
                    room,
                    name,
                    mode,
                    actor,
                    master,
                    data,
                    tick_hz,
                    schema_hash,
                    ..
                })) => {
                    break Joined {
                        room,
                        name,
                        mode,
                        actor,
                        master,
                        tick_hz,
                        schema_hash,
                        data,
                    };
                }
                Some(Event::Control(ServerMsg::Error { code, message })) => {
                    return Err(ClientError::Server { code, message })
                }
                Some(Event::Closed(_)) | None => return Err(ClientError::Disconnected),
                _ => continue,
            }
        };
        self.open_data(&joined.data).await?;
        self.joined = Some(joined.clone());
        Ok(joined)
    }

    async fn open_data(&mut self, ep: &DataEndpoint) -> Result<()> {
        let ticket = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD
            .decode(&ep.ticket)
            .map_err(|e| ClientError::Data(e.to_string()))?;
        let link = Mutex::new(Link::new(Instant::now()));
        let dp: Arc<DataPath> = if self.opts.tunnel {
            let (ws_tx, mut ws_rx) = mpsc::channel::<Message>(1024);
            let ctl = self.ctl.clone();
            self.tasks.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
                while let Some(m) = ws_rx.recv().await {
                    if ctl.send(m).await.is_err() {
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }));
            let dp = Arc::new(DataPath {
                link,
                sink: Sink::Ws(ws_tx),
            });
            // Register before sending the ticket: the server's ack may arrive immediately.
            if let Some(slot) = &self.tunnel_slot {
                *slot.lock() = Some(dp.clone());
            }
            self.ctl
                .send(Message::Binary(ticket.into()))
                .await
                .map_err(|_| ClientError::Disconnected)?;
            dp
        } else {
            let transport = quic::transport_config(Duration::from_secs(15), Duration::from_secs(5));
            let endpoint =
                quic::client_endpoint("0.0.0.0:0".parse().unwrap(), &ep.cert_sha256, transport)
                    .map_err(|e| ClientError::Data(e.to_string()))?;
            let addr = tokio::net::lookup_host((ep.host.as_str(), ep.port))
                .await
                .map_err(|e| ClientError::Data(e.to_string()))?
                .find(|a| a.is_ipv4())
                .ok_or_else(|| ClientError::Data("no address".into()))?;
            let conn = tokio::time::timeout(self.opts.connect_timeout, async {
                endpoint
                    .connect(addr, "aurix-net")
                    .map_err(|e| ClientError::Data(e.to_string()))?
                    .await
                    .map_err(|e| ClientError::Data(e.to_string()))
            })
            .await
            .map_err(|_| ClientError::Timeout)??;
            conn.send_datagram(Bytes::from(ticket))
                .map_err(|e| ClientError::Data(e.to_string()))?;
            let dp = Arc::new(DataPath {
                link,
                sink: Sink::Quic(conn.clone()),
            });
            let (dp2, ev) = (dp.clone(), self.events_tx.clone());
            self.tasks.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
                while let Ok(d) = conn.read_datagram().await {
                    deliver(&dp2, d, &ev).await;
                }
                let _ = ev.send(Event::Closed("data path closed".into())).await;
            }));
            dp
        };
        // link timer
        let (dp2, tick) = (dp.clone(), self.opts.tick);
        self.tasks.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut iv = tokio::time::interval(tick);
            loop {
                iv.tick().await;
                if dp2.link.lock().poll(Instant::now()).is_err() {
                    break;
                }
                dp2.flush();
            }
        }));
        self.data = Some(dp);
        // wait for the server's empty ack frame
        let deadline = Instant::now() + self.opts.connect_timeout;
        loop {
            match tokio::time::timeout_at(deadline.into(), self.next_event()).await {
                Ok(Some(Event::DataReady)) => return Ok(()),
                Ok(Some(Event::Closed(_))) | Ok(None) => return Err(ClientError::Disconnected),
                Ok(Some(_)) => continue,
                Err(_) => return Err(ClientError::Timeout),
            }
        }
    }

    /// Queues a data-path message; unreliable messages leave on the next timer tick (or
    /// immediately with `flush`).
    pub fn send_data(&self, channel: Channel, payload: Bytes) -> Result<()> {
        let dp = self.data.as_ref().ok_or(ClientError::Disconnected)?;
        dp.link
            .lock()
            .send(channel, payload, Instant::now())
            .map_err(|e| ClientError::Data(format!("{e:?}")))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Pushes everything queued onto the wire now (call once per game frame).
    pub fn flush(&self) {
        if let Some(dp) = &self.data {
            dp.link.lock().flush_batch();
            dp.flush();
        }
    }

    /// Relay helper: raise an event.
    pub fn send_event(
        &self,
        code: u8,
        target: EventTarget,
        payload: Bytes,
        reliable: bool,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let frame = EventFrame {
            code,
            target,
            cache: CacheOp::None,
            group: None,
            from: net_common::ActorId(0),
            payload,
        };
        self.send_data(
            if reliable {
                Channel::ReliableOrdered
            } else {
                Channel::UnreliableSequenced
            },
            frame.encode(),
        )
    }

    pub async fn next_event(&mut self) -> Option<Event> {
        self.events.recv().await
    }

    /// Non-blocking poll for engines with their own loop.
    pub fn try_next_event(&mut self) -> Option<Event> {
        self.events.try_recv().ok()
    }

    pub fn link_stats(&self) -> Option<net_transport::LinkStats> {
        self.data.as_ref().map(|d| d.link.lock().stats())
    }

    pub async fn leave(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        self.send(ClientMsg::Leave).await
    }

    /// Ask for project-wide room/player counts per lobby; the answer arrives as
    /// `Event::Control(ServerMsg::Stats { .. })`. At most one `stats`/`find_friends` per second.
    pub async fn stats(&self) -> Result<()> {
        self.send(ClientMsg::Stats).await
    }

    /// Ask where up to 64 players are (online, room) across the fleet; the answer arrives as
    /// `Event::Control(ServerMsg::Friends { .. })`.
    pub async fn find_friends(&self, players: Vec<String>) -> Result<()> {
        self.send(ClientMsg::FindFriends { players }).await
    }
    /// Call the game's backend through the node (the project's `rpc` webhook); the answer
    /// arrives as `Event::Control(ServerMsg::RpcResult { id, .. })`. Body ≤ 8 KiB, 5 per second.
    pub async fn rpc(
        &self,
        id: u32,
        name: impl Into<String>,
        body: serde_json::Value,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        self.send(ClientMsg::Rpc {
            id,
            name: name.into(),
            body,
        })
        .await
    }

    /// Sync rooms: steer area-of-interest — extra viewpoints (camera, scope target) and entities
    /// forced into view (team mates, objectives). Entity ids as in deltas.
    pub async fn set_view(&mut self, viewpoints: Vec<u64>, interest: Vec<u64>) -> Result<()> {
        self.send(ClientMsg::SetView {
            viewpoints,
            interest,
        })
        .await
    }
}

impl Drop for Client {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        for t in &self.tasks {
            t.abort();
        }
        if let Some(dp) = &self.data {
            if let Sink::Quic(c) = &dp.sink {
                c.close(0u32.into(), b"bye");
            }
        }
    }
}

async fn deliver(dp: &Arc<DataPath>, d: Bytes, ev: &mpsc::Sender<Event>) {
    let recv = dp.link.lock().receive(d, Instant::now());
    dp.flush();
    for m in recv {
        if m.payload.is_empty() {
            let _ = ev.send(Event::DataReady).await;
            continue;
        }
        if ev
            .send(Event::Data {
                channel: m.channel,
                tick: m.tick,
                payload: m.payload,
            })
            .await
            .is_err()
        {
            return;
        }
    }
}

```

`crates/net-client/src/lockstep.rs`:

```rs
//! Client side of lockstep rooms, the same core as the managed (C#) and Web SDKs: confirmed input
//! bundles delivered in tick order, late-join catch-up, hash reports, checkpoint uploads when the
//! node asks the master, adaptive input delay from the node's margin reports and state dumps after a
//! desync. Pure logic: feed every data-path payload to [`LockstepClient::receive`], send the frames
//! it hands back. The game owns the deterministic simulation.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use bytes::{BufMut, Bytes, BytesMut};

pub const LS_INPUT: u8 = 0x10;
pub const LS_BUNDLE: u8 = 0x20;
pub const LS_HASH: u8 = 0x21;
pub const LS_CHECKPOINT: u8 = 0x22;
pub const LS_CHECKPOINT_REQ: u8 = 0x23;
pub const LS_CATCHUP: u8 = 0x24;
pub const LS_INPUT_STATS: u8 = 0x25;
pub const LS_DUMP_REQ: u8 = 0x26;
pub const LS_DUMP: u8 = 0x27;

/// Ticks of future bundles kept while waiting for a gap to fill before they are dropped.
const MAX_PENDING_AHEAD: u32 = 600;

/// Confirmed inputs of one tick: actor id → input bytes (absent actor = sent nothing).
pub type TickInputs = BTreeMap<u16, Bytes>;

/// What the node told us, in order. `Tick` arrives for every tick exactly once.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum LsEvent {
    Tick {
        tick: u32,
        inputs: TickInputs,
    },
    /// Catch-up start: restore the game from this checkpoint (empty state at tick 0 = fresh start).
    Restore {
        tick: u32,
        hash: u64,
        state: Bytes,
    },
    /// The node asked us (the master) for the confirmed state at a tick <= this one: answer with
    /// [`LockstepClient::checkpoint_frame`].
    CheckpointRequested(u32),
    /// The node flagged a desync and wants our state at this tick: answer with
    /// [`LockstepClient::dump_frame`] or ignore.
    DumpRequested(u32),
}

/// A frame to send on the data path; `reliable` picks the channel.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Outgoing {
    pub reliable: bool,
    pub payload: Bytes,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct LockstepClient {
    pending: BTreeMap<u32, TickInputs>,
    recent_inputs: Vec<Bytes>,
    started: bool,
    next: u32,
    last_input: u32,
    slack_streak: u8,
    /// Newest tick the node has bundled (+1).
    pub server_tick: u32,
    /// Ticks ahead of the server clock inputs are stamped; tuned between min/max from margin
    /// reports when `adaptive_delay` is on.
    pub input_delay: u32,
    pub input_delay_min: u32,
    pub input_delay_max: u32,
    pub adaptive_delay: bool,
    /// Inputs repeated per datagram (1..=8).
    pub input_redundancy: usize,
    pub last_margin: i8,
    pub late_inputs: u64,
    pub delivered: u64,
    pub catchups: u64,
    pub dropped: u64,
}

impl Default for LockstepClient {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl LockstepClient {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            pending: BTreeMap::new(),
            recent_inputs: Vec::new(),
            started: false,
            next: 0,
            last_input: 0,
            slack_streak: 0,
            server_tick: 0,
            input_delay: 2,
            input_delay_min: 1,
            input_delay_max: 8,
            adaptive_delay: true,
            input_redundancy: 3,
            last_margin: 0,
            late_inputs: 0,
            delivered: 0,
            catchups: 0,
            dropped: 0,
        }
    }

    /// Next tick to be delivered as `LsEvent::Tick`.
    pub fn confirmed_tick(&self) -> u32 {
        self.next
    }

    /// Feeds one data-path payload. `None` when it was not a lockstep frame.
    pub fn receive(&mut self, p: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<LsEvent>> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        match *p.first()? {
            LS_CATCHUP => {
                if p.len() >= 17 {
                    let tick = u32_at(p, 1);
                    let hash = u64_at(p, 5);
                    let len = (u32_at(p, 13) as usize).min(p.len() - 17);
                    self.pending.clear();
                    self.next = tick;
                    self.started = true;
                    self.catchups += 1;
                    out.push(LsEvent::Restore {
                        tick,
                        hash,
                        state: Bytes::copy_from_slice(&p[17..17 + len]),
                    });
                }
            }
            LS_BUNDLE => {
                if p.len() >= 2 {
                    let n = p[1] as usize;
                    let mut o = 2;
                    for _ in 0..n {
                        if o + 2 > p.len() {
                            break;
                        }
                        let len = u16::from_be_bytes([p[o], p[o + 1]]) as usize;
                        o += 2;
                        if o + len > p.len() {
                            break;
                        }
                        self.decode_bundle(&p[o..o + len]);
                        o += len;
                    }
                    self.drain(&mut out);
                }
            }
            LS_CHECKPOINT_REQ => {
                if p.len() >= 5 {
                    out.push(LsEvent::CheckpointRequested(u32_at(p, 1)));
                }
            }
            LS_DUMP_REQ => {
                if p.len() >= 5 {
                    out.push(LsEvent::DumpRequested(u32_at(p, 1)));
                }
            }
            LS_INPUT_STATS => {
                if p.len() >= 7 {
                    self.on_input_stats(p[5] as i8, p[6]);
                }
            }
            LS_CHECKPOINT | LS_HASH | LS_INPUT => {}
            _ => return None,
        }
        Some(out)
    }

    /// Raises the delay as soon as inputs arrive late; lowers it one tick after three consecutive
    /// reports with >= 2 ticks of slack.
    pub fn on_input_stats(&mut self, margin: i8, late: u8) {
        self.last_margin = margin;
        self.late_inputs += late as u64;
        if !self.adaptive_delay {
            return;
        }
        if margin < 0 {
            let bump = (-(margin as i32)).min(4) as u32;
            self.input_delay = (self.input_delay + bump).min(self.input_delay_max);
            self.slack_streak = 0;
        } else if margin >= 2 {
            self.slack_streak += 1;
            if self.slack_streak >= 3 {
                self.slack_streak = 0;
                if self.input_delay > self.input_delay_min {
                    self.input_delay -= 1;
                }
            }
        } else {
            self.slack_streak = 0;
        }
    }

    fn decode_bundle(&mut self, b: &[u8]) {
        if b.len() < 6 || b[0] != LS_BUNDLE {
            return;
        }
        let t = u32_at(b, 1);
        let k = b[5] as usize;
        let mut o = 6;
        self.server_tick = self.server_tick.max(t + 1);
        if !self.started {
            self.started = true;
            self.next = t;
        }
        if t < self.next || self.pending.contains_key(&t) {
            return;
        }
        let mut inputs = TickInputs::new();
        for _ in 0..k {
            if o + 3 > b.len() {
                break;
            }
            let a = u16::from_be_bytes([b[o], b[o + 1]]);
            let l = b[o + 2] as usize;
            o += 3;
            if o + l > b.len() {
                break;
            }
            inputs.insert(a, Bytes::copy_from_slice(&b[o..o + l]));
            o += l;
        }
        self.pending.insert(t, inputs);
    }

    fn drain(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<LsEvent>) {
        while let Some(inputs) = self.pending.remove(&self.next) {
            let tick = self.next;
            self.next += 1;
            self.delivered += 1;
            out.push(LsEvent::Tick { tick, inputs });
        }
        let limit = self.next + MAX_PENDING_AHEAD;
        let far: Vec<u32> = self.pending.range(limit + 1..).map(|(t, _)| *t).collect();
        self.dropped += far.len() as u64;
        for t in far {
            self.pending.remove(&t);
        }
    }

    /// Queues this tick's local input (sent together with the previous ones for redundancy).
    /// Returns the tick it was stamped with and the unreliable frame to send.
    pub fn send_input(&mut self, input: Bytes) -> (u32, Outgoing) {
        let tick = (self.server_tick + self.input_delay).max(self.last_input + 1);
        self.last_input = tick;
        self.recent_inputs.push(input);
        let keep = self.input_redundancy.clamp(1, 8);
        while self.recent_inputs.len() > keep {
            self.recent_inputs.remove(0);
        }
        let first = tick - (self.recent_inputs.len() as u32 - 1);
        let mut b = BytesMut::with_capacity(
            6 + self
                .recent_inputs
                .iter()
                .map(|i| i.len() + 1)
                .sum::<usize>(),
        );
        b.put_u8(LS_INPUT);
        b.put_u32(first);
        b.put_u8(self.recent_inputs.len() as u8);
        for i in &self.recent_inputs {
            b.put_u8(i.len().min(255) as u8);
            b.extend_from_slice(&i[..i.len().min(255)]);
        }
        (
            tick,
            Outgoing {
                reliable: false,
                payload: b.freeze(),
            },
        )
    }

    /// Hash of the confirmed state after `tick`; the node compares it across players (and the
    /// server simulation when there is one).
    pub fn hash_frame(tick: u32, hash: u64) -> Outgoing {
        let mut b = BytesMut::with_capacity(13);
        b.put_u8(LS_HASH);
        b.put_u32(tick);
        b.put_u64(hash);
        Outgoing {
            reliable: false,
            payload: b.freeze(),
        }
    }

    /// Master only, in answer to `CheckpointRequested`: confirmed state at `tick` (<= requested).
    pub fn checkpoint_frame(tick: u32, hash: u64, state: &[u8]) -> Outgoing {
        frame(LS_CHECKPOINT, tick, hash, state)
    }

    /// Answer to `DumpRequested`: your state at `tick` (<= 60 KiB), kept by the node for 24 h next
    /// to the master's for offline diffing.
    pub fn dump_frame(tick: u32, hash: u64, state: &[u8]) -> Outgoing {
        frame(LS_DUMP, tick, hash, state)
    }

    /// FNV-1a 64 over bytes: the portable state hash the other SDKs use.
    pub fn fnv1a(data: &[u8]) -> u64 {
        data.iter().fold(0xcbf29ce484222325u64, |h, &x| {
            (h ^ x as u64).wrapping_mul(0x100000001b3)
        })
    }
}

fn frame(kind: u8, tick: u32, hash: u64, state: &[u8]) -> Outgoing {
    let mut b = BytesMut::with_capacity(13 + state.len());
    b.put_u8(kind);
    b.put_u32(tick);
    b.put_u64(hash);
    b.extend_from_slice(state);
    Outgoing {
        reliable: true,
        payload: b.freeze(),
    }
}

fn u32_at(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_be_bytes([b[o], b[o + 1], b[o + 2], b[o + 3]])
}

fn u64_at(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> u64 {
    ((u32_at(b, o) as u64) << 32) | u32_at(b, o + 4) as u64
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    type TickSpec<'a> = (u32, &'a [(u16, &'a [u8])]);

    fn bundle(ticks: &[TickSpec<'_>]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut p = vec![LS_BUNDLE, ticks.len() as u8];
        for (t, inputs) in ticks {
            let mut b = vec![LS_BUNDLE];
            b.extend_from_slice(&t.to_be_bytes());
            b.push(inputs.len() as u8);
            for (a, d) in *inputs {
                b.extend_from_slice(&a.to_be_bytes());
                b.push(d.len() as u8);
                b.extend_from_slice(d);
            }
            p.extend_from_slice(&(b.len() as u16).to_be_bytes());
            p.extend_from_slice(&b);
        }
        p
    }

    #[test]
    fn bundles_are_delivered_in_tick_order_and_once() {
        let mut c = LockstepClient::new();
        let ev = c.receive(&bundle(&[(0, &[(1, b"a")])])).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ev.len(), 1);
        assert!(matches!(&ev[0], LsEvent::Tick { tick: 0, inputs } if inputs[&1].as_ref() == b"a"));
        // tick 2 before tick 1: held back, then both delivered in order
        assert!(c.receive(&bundle(&[(2, &[])])).unwrap().is_empty());
        let ev = c.receive(&bundle(&[(1, &[(2, b"xy")]), (0, &[])])).unwrap();
        let ticks: Vec<u32> = ev
            .iter()
            .map(|e| match e {
                LsEvent::Tick { tick, .. } => *tick,
                _ => unreachable!(),
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(ticks, vec![1, 2]);
        assert_eq!(c.confirmed_tick(), 3);
        assert_eq!(c.server_tick, 3);
        assert_eq!(c.delivered, 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn catchup_restores_and_resets_the_cursor() {
        let mut c = LockstepClient::new();
        c.receive(&bundle(&[(0, &[])])).unwrap();
        let mut p = vec![LS_CATCHUP];
        p.extend_from_slice(&40u32.to_be_bytes());
        p.extend_from_slice(&7u64.to_be_bytes());
        p.extend_from_slice(&3u32.to_be_bytes());
        p.extend_from_slice(b"abc");
        let ev = c.receive(&p).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            ev,
            vec![LsEvent::Restore {
                tick: 40,
                hash: 7,
                state: Bytes::from_static(b"abc")
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!(c.confirmed_tick(), 40);
        assert!(c.receive(&bundle(&[(39, &[])])).unwrap().is_empty());
        assert_eq!(c.receive(&bundle(&[(40, &[])])).unwrap().len(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn input_frames_carry_redundant_inputs_and_adaptive_delay() {
        let mut c = LockstepClient::new();
        c.input_redundancy = 2;
        c.server_tick = 10;
        let (t1, _) = c.send_input(Bytes::from_static(b"A"));
        assert_eq!(t1, 12);
        let (t2, f) = c.send_input(Bytes::from_static(b"BB"));
        assert_eq!(t2, 13);
        assert!(!f.reliable);
        assert_eq!(
            f.payload.as_ref(),
            &[LS_INPUT, 0, 0, 0, 12, 2, 1, b'A', 2, b'B', b'B']
        );
        // late report: delay jumps; three slack reports: delay drops by one
        c.receive(&[LS_INPUT_STATS, 0, 0, 0, 30, 0xFE, 1]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((c.input_delay, c.last_margin, c.late_inputs), (4, -2, 1));
        for _ in 0..3 {
            c.receive(&[LS_INPUT_STATS, 0, 0, 0, 60, 3, 0]).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(c.input_delay, 3);
        c.input_delay_max = 4;
        c.on_input_stats(-100, 0);
        assert_eq!(c.input_delay, 4);
        c.adaptive_delay = false;
        c.on_input_stats(-5, 2);
        assert_eq!((c.input_delay, c.late_inputs), (4, 3));
    }

    #[test]
    fn requests_and_answer_frames() {
        let mut c = LockstepClient::new();
        assert_eq!(
            c.receive(&[LS_CHECKPOINT_REQ, 0, 0, 1, 0]).unwrap(),
            vec![LsEvent::CheckpointRequested(256)]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            c.receive(&[LS_DUMP_REQ, 0, 0, 0, 9]).unwrap(),
            vec![LsEvent::DumpRequested(9)]
        );
        assert_eq!(c.receive(&[0x11, 1, 2]), None);
        let d = LockstepClient::dump_frame(9, 0x0102030405060708, b"st");
        assert!(d.reliable);
        assert_eq!(
            d.payload.as_ref(),
            &[LS_DUMP, 0, 0, 0, 9, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, b's', b't']
        );
        assert_eq!(LockstepClient::hash_frame(1, 2).payload.len(), 13);
        assert_eq!(LockstepClient::fnv1a(b""), 0xcbf29ce484222325);
        assert_eq!(LockstepClient::fnv1a(b"a"), 0xaf63dc4c8601ec8c);
    }
}
```

`crates/net-client/src/rollback.rs`:

```rs
//! Predict/rollback on top of lockstep: the game runs ahead of the confirmed tick with predicted
//! remote inputs (each actor's last confirmed input, repeated) and its own inputs as sent, keeps a
//! snapshot per predicted tick, and when the node confirms a tick whose inputs differ from the
//! prediction it restores the snapshot, re-steps that tick and re-predicts the ticks after it.
//! Local actions therefore render immediately; the simulation stays deterministic because only
//! confirmed inputs ever reach the confirmed state. Same core as the C#/Web `LockstepRollback`.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use bytes::Bytes;

use crate::lockstep::TickInputs;

/// The game's deterministic simulation: step by one tick, snapshot and restore.
pub trait Simulation {
    type Snapshot;
    fn step(&mut self, tick: u32, inputs: &TickInputs);
    fn snapshot(&self) -> Self::Snapshot;
    fn restore(&mut self, s: &Self::Snapshot);
}

pub struct Rollback<S: Simulation> {
    local_actor: u16,
    /// Ticks the simulation may run ahead of the confirmed tick.
    pub max_prediction: u32,
    /// First tick not yet confirmed by the node.
    confirmed: u32,
    /// Next tick to simulate (confirmed..head are predicted).
    head: u32,
    /// Snapshot of the state *before* tick t, for every t in confirmed..=head.
    history: BTreeMap<u32, S::Snapshot>,
    predicted: BTreeMap<u32, TickInputs>,
    local_inputs: BTreeMap<u32, Bytes>,
    /// Newest input we sent: the guess for local ticks not yet stamped.
    last_local: Option<Bytes>,
    last_known: TickInputs,
    pub rollbacks: u64,
    pub resimulated_ticks: u64,
    pub predicted_ticks: u64,
}

impl<S: Simulation> Rollback<S> {
    /// `sim` must be at tick `start` (fresh game, or restored from a catch-up checkpoint).
    pub fn new(sim: &S, local_actor: u16, start: u32, max_prediction: u32) -> Self {
        let mut history = BTreeMap::new();
        history.insert(start, sim.snapshot());
        Self {
            local_actor,
            max_prediction: max_prediction.max(1),
            confirmed: start,
            head: start,
            history,
            predicted: BTreeMap::new(),
            local_inputs: BTreeMap::new(),
            last_local: None,
            last_known: TickInputs::new(),
            rollbacks: 0,
            resimulated_ticks: 0,
            predicted_ticks: 0,
        }
    }

    /// After the game restored a catch-up checkpoint at `tick`: forget every prediction.
    pub fn reset(&mut self, sim: &S, tick: u32) {
        self.history.clear();
        self.history.insert(tick, sim.snapshot());
        self.predicted.clear();
        self.local_inputs.clear();
        self.confirmed = tick;
        self.head = tick;
    }

    pub fn confirmed_tick(&self) -> u32 {
        self.confirmed
    }

    /// State after the last confirmed tick: hash *this* for `hash_frame`, never the predicted head.
    pub fn confirmed_snapshot(&self) -> &S::Snapshot {
        &self.history[&self.confirmed]
    }

    /// Next tick the simulation will run; `head() - confirmed_tick()` ticks are predicted.
    pub fn head(&self) -> u32 {
        self.head
    }

    /// Remember the input we sent stamped with `tick` (the value `LockstepClient::send_input`
    /// returned) so our own prediction uses exactly it.
    pub fn local_input(&mut self, tick: u32, input: Bytes) {
        self.last_local = Some(input.clone());
        self.local_inputs.insert(tick, input);
    }

    /// Runs the simulation ahead to `target` (exclusive), bounded by `max_prediction`.
    pub fn predict(&mut self, sim: &mut S, target: u32) {
        let target = target.min(self.confirmed + self.max_prediction);
        while self.head < target {
            let t = self.head;
            let inputs = self.guess(t);
            sim.step(t, &inputs);
            self.predicted.insert(t, inputs);
            self.head = t + 1;
            self.history.insert(self.head, sim.snapshot());
            self.predicted_ticks += 1;
        }
    }

    /// Feeds a confirmed tick (`LsEvent::Tick`). Returns true when a rollback happened.
    pub fn confirm(&mut self, sim: &mut S, tick: u32, inputs: &TickInputs) -> bool {
        if tick != self.confirmed {
            return false;
        }
        for (a, i) in inputs {
            self.last_known.insert(*a, i.clone());
        }
        self.local_inputs.remove(&tick);
        let mut rolled = false;
        if tick >= self.head {
            sim.step(tick, inputs);
            self.head = tick + 1;
            self.history.insert(self.head, sim.snapshot());
        } else if self.predicted.get(&tick) != Some(inputs) {
            rolled = true;
            self.rollbacks += 1;
            let before = self
                .history
                .get(&tick)
                .expect("snapshot before every predicted tick");
            sim.restore(before);
            sim.step(tick, inputs);
            self.history.insert(tick + 1, sim.snapshot());
            let old_head = self.head;
            self.head = tick + 1;
            self.predicted.split_off(&(tick + 1));
            self.resimulated_ticks += (old_head - self.head) as u64;
            self.predict(sim, old_head);
        }
        self.confirmed = tick + 1;
        self.predicted.remove(&tick);
        self.history.remove(&tick);
        rolled
    }

    fn guess(&self, tick: u32) -> TickInputs {
        let mut g = self.last_known.clone();
        match self.local_inputs.get(&tick).or(self.last_local.as_ref()) {
            Some(i) => {
                g.insert(self.local_actor, i.clone());
            }
            None => {
                g.remove(&self.local_actor);
            }
        }
        g
    }
}

/// Instant replay (kill cam) buffer: the last `keep` confirmed ticks' inputs plus a snapshot of the
/// confirmed state every `every` ticks, so any recent moment can be re-simulated locally without
/// asking the node. Feed it from the confirmed path (`confirm` + `confirmed_snapshot`).
pub struct ReplayRing<S> {
    keep: u32,
    every: u32,
    /// Tick of `inputs[0]`.
    first: u32,
    inputs: std::collections::VecDeque<TickInputs>,
    /// State *before* tick `k` for boundaries `k` that are multiples of `every` (and the first one).
    snaps: BTreeMap<u32, S>,
}

/// What `ReplayRing::window` hands back: restore `snapshot`, then step `inputs` from `start`.
pub struct ReplayWindow<'a, S> {
    pub start: u32,
    pub snapshot: &'a S,
    pub inputs: Vec<&'a TickInputs>,
}

impl<S> ReplayRing<S> {
    pub fn new(keep_ticks: u32, snapshot_every: u32) -> Self {
        Self {
            keep: keep_ticks.max(1),
            every: snapshot_every.max(1),
            first: 0,
            inputs: std::collections::VecDeque::new(),
            snaps: BTreeMap::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Records confirmed `tick` with its inputs and the confirmed state *before* it (taken lazily
    /// only on snapshot boundaries). Ticks must arrive in order; a gap resets the ring.
    pub fn record(&mut self, tick: u32, inputs: TickInputs, state_before: impl FnOnce() -> S) {
        if self.inputs.is_empty() || self.first + self.inputs.len() as u32 != tick {
            self.inputs.clear();
            self.snaps.clear();
            self.first = tick;
        }
        if self.snaps.is_empty() || tick.is_multiple_of(self.every) {
            self.snaps.insert(tick, state_before());
        }
        self.inputs.push_back(inputs);
        while self.inputs.len() as u32 > self.keep {
            self.inputs.pop_front();
            self.first += 1;
        }
        // keep the newest snapshot at or before `first`, drop older ones
        if let Some((&anchor, _)) = self.snaps.range(..=self.first).next_back() {
            self.snaps.retain(|k, _| *k >= anchor);
        }
    }

    /// Oldest tick that can still be replayed.
    pub fn oldest(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        self.snaps
            .keys()
            .next()
            .copied()
            .filter(|_| !self.inputs.is_empty())
    }

    /// Everything needed to re-simulate from the newest snapshot at or before `from` (clamped to
    /// what is kept) through the last recorded tick.
    pub fn window(&self, from: u32) -> Option<ReplayWindow<'_, S>> {
        let (&start, snapshot) = self
            .snaps
            .range(..=from)
            .next_back()
            .or_else(|| self.snaps.iter().next())?;
        let skip = start.saturating_sub(self.first) as usize;
        let inputs = self.inputs.iter().skip(skip).collect();
        Some(ReplayWindow {
            start,
            snapshot,
            inputs,
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    #[test]
    fn replay_ring_rewinds_from_the_nearest_snapshot() {
        let mut ring: ReplayRing<u32> = ReplayRing::new(50, 10);
        for t in 0..100u32 {
            ring.record(t, inputs(&[(1, t as u8)]), || t * 100);
        }
        let w = ring.window(73).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((w.start, *w.snapshot, w.inputs.len()), (70, 7000, 30));
        assert_eq!(w.inputs[0][&1].as_ref(), &[70]);
        // older than what is kept: clamps to the oldest snapshot that still has all its inputs
        let w = ring.window(5).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((w.start, w.inputs.len()), (50, 50));
        assert_eq!(ring.oldest(), Some(50));
        // a gap resets
        ring.record(200, inputs(&[]), || 1);
        assert_eq!(
            (ring.oldest(), ring.window(0).unwrap().inputs.len()),
            (Some(200), 1)
        );
    }

    use super::*;

    /// Order-sensitive toy sim: state = fold over (tick, actor, input byte).
    #[derive(Default, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
    struct Toy {
        state: u64,
        steps: u64,
    }
    impl Simulation for Toy {
        type Snapshot = Toy;
        fn step(&mut self, tick: u32, inputs: &TickInputs) {
            for (a, i) in inputs {
                let b = i.first().copied().unwrap_or(0) as u64;
                self.state = self
                    .state
                    .wrapping_mul(31)
                    .wrapping_add(tick as u64 * 1000 + *a as u64 * 10 + b);
            }
            self.state = self.state.wrapping_mul(7).wrapping_add(tick as u64);
            self.steps += 1;
        }
        fn snapshot(&self) -> Toy {
            self.clone()
        }
        fn restore(&mut self, s: &Toy) {
            *self = s.clone();
        }
    }

    fn inputs(v: &[(u16, u8)]) -> TickInputs {
        v.iter().map(|(a, b)| (*a, Bytes::from(vec![*b]))).collect()
    }

    fn reference(script: &[TickInputs]) -> u64 {
        let mut s = Toy::default();
        for (t, i) in script.iter().enumerate() {
            s.step(t as u32, i);
        }
        s.state
    }

    #[test]
    fn correct_predictions_never_roll_back() {
        let mut sim = Toy::default();
        let mut rb = Rollback::new(&sim, 1, 0, 8);
        let script: Vec<TickInputs> = (0..10).map(|_| inputs(&[(1, 5), (2, 9)])).collect();
        rb.confirm(&mut sim, 0, &script[0]);
        for t in 1..10u32 {
            rb.local_input(t, Bytes::from(vec![5]));
            rb.predict(&mut sim, t + 3);
            assert!(!rb.confirm(&mut sim, t, &script[t as usize]));
        }
        assert_eq!(rb.rollbacks, 0);
        assert_eq!(rb.confirmed_tick(), 10);
        // head ran ahead; the confirmed snapshot equals a pure confirmed simulation
        sim.restore(rb.confirmed_snapshot());
        assert_eq!(sim.state, reference(&script));
    }

    #[test]
    fn mispredicted_remote_input_rolls_back_to_the_same_state_as_pure_lockstep() {
        let mut sim = Toy::default();
        let mut rb = Rollback::new(&sim, 1, 0, 8);
        let mut script: Vec<TickInputs> = (0..8).map(|_| inputs(&[(1, 1), (2, 2)])).collect();
        script[4] = inputs(&[(1, 1), (2, 7)]); // remote actor changes input at tick 4
        script[5] = inputs(&[(2, 7)]); // and our own input arrives late (dropped from tick 5)
        for t in 0..8u32 {
            rb.local_input(t, Bytes::from(vec![1]));
            rb.predict(&mut sim, t + 4);
            rb.confirm(&mut sim, t, &script[t as usize]);
        }
        // ticks 0 (actor 2 unknown yet), 4, 5 and 6: identical across the Rust/Web/C# cores
        assert_eq!(rb.rollbacks, 4);
        assert!(rb.resimulated_ticks > 0);
        sim.restore(rb.confirmed_snapshot());
        assert_eq!(sim.state, reference(&script));
        assert_eq!(rb.head(), 11);
    }

    #[test]
    fn prediction_is_bounded_and_reset_forgets_history() {
        let mut sim = Toy::default();
        let mut rb = Rollback::new(&sim, 1, 0, 3);
        rb.predict(&mut sim, 100);
        assert_eq!(rb.head(), 3);
        assert_eq!(rb.predicted_ticks, 3);
        assert!(
            !rb.confirm(&mut sim, 7, &inputs(&[])),
            "out-of-order confirm is ignored"
        );
        sim = Toy {
            state: 42,
            steps: 0,
        };
        rb.reset(&sim, 50);
        assert_eq!((rb.confirmed_tick(), rb.head()), (50, 50));
        rb.predict(&mut sim, 52);
        assert_eq!(rb.head(), 52);
        assert_eq!(rb.history.len(), 3);
    }
}
```

`crates/net-client/tests/garbage.rs`:

```rs
//! The lockstep client never panics on garbage from the node.
use net_client::lockstep::LockstepClient;
fn rng(seed: u64) -> impl FnMut() -> u64 {
    let mut s = seed | 1;
    move || {
        s ^= s << 13;
        s ^= s >> 7;
        s ^= s << 17;
        s
    }
}
fn garbage(r: &mut impl FnMut() -> u64, max: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let n = (r() as usize) % (max + 1);
    (0..n).map(|_| r() as u8).collect()
}
#[allow(dead_code)]
fn mutate(r: &mut impl FnMut() -> u64, v: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut m = v.to_vec();
    let k = 1 + (r() % 4) as usize;
    for _ in 0..k {
        if m.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        let i = (r() as usize) % m.len();
        match r() % 3 {
            0 => m[i] ^= 1 << (r() % 8),
            1 => {
                m.remove(i);
            }
            _ => m.insert(i, r() as u8),
        }
    }
    m
}
#[test]
fn lockstep_client_receive_survives_garbage() {
    let mut r = rng(23);
    let mut c = LockstepClient::new();
    for _ in 0..20_000 {
        let mut g = garbage(&mut r, 96);
        if r().is_multiple_of(2) && !g.is_empty() {
            g[0] = [0x20u8, 0x21, 0x22, 0x23, 0x24, 0x25, 0x26, 0x27][(r() as usize) % 8];
        }
        let _ = c.receive(&g);
    }
}
```

```rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct NetConfig {
    pub server: ServerConfig,
    pub transport: TransportConfig,
    pub database: DatabaseConfig,
    pub redis: RedisConfig,
    pub auth: AuthConfig,
    pub limits: LimitsConfig,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub retention: RetentionConfig,
}

/// How long closed rows stay in Postgres before the hourly janitor deletes them (0 = keep forever).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct RetentionConfig {
    #[serde(default = "d_closed_rooms_days")]
    pub closed_rooms_days: u32,
    #[serde(default = "d_audit_days")]
    pub audit_days: u32,
    /// Billing rows (`usage_hours`); keep well past your invoicing window.
    #[serde(default = "d_usage_days")]
    pub usage_days: u32,
    /// Webhook delivery log rows.
    #[serde(default = "d_webhook_deliveries_days")]
    pub webhook_deliveries_days: u32,
}

fn d_webhook_deliveries_days() -> u32 {
    7
}

impl Default for RetentionConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            closed_rooms_days: d_closed_rooms_days(),
            audit_days: d_audit_days(),
            usage_days: d_usage_days(),
            webhook_deliveries_days: d_webhook_deliveries_days(),
        }
    }
}
```
